title: Play pass 4 — answer the Phase 2 exit question
description:
The Phase 2 exit question is: is spending a hero's life a decision you actually feel? Unanswered after three play passes. This is not a code ticket — it is someone sitting down and playing the built game.

docs/TASKS.md has been saying this is the real next move for three sessions. The user's own sequencing was models first, then play; the models (P2b-09/P2b-10) have landed.

What a pass must cover, because no pass has ever met them: training, traits, buildings, gear recovery, and everything the fe1a74b arena/hub batch added. The 22 PROVISIONAL arena feel values have been played once as a whole (verdict: 'feels good for what it is') but never felt individually.

If the answer is no, the fix is design, not code.

Reference: docs/TASKS.md 'Phase 2 exit question' section, and the superseded handoff comment above it.
close_reason: Played. Answer: yes, spending a hero's life is a felt decision. Remaining gap is animation/combat feel, which is clunky; the two P1 feel tickets are now unblocked.

title: A new town can lock forever: three Lumbermills first leave no wood for a House
description:
WHY
Found by extra in the ig-6m2.3 deadlock check (2026-09-24). This is live today. The town starts with 40 wood and the first Lumbermill is free. Two more Lumbermills at 20 each spend all 40, and there is no House.
- A worker needs a House: station_hero refuses with "needs a house before working".
- Wood only comes from Lumbermill workers at home (game_session.gd _advance_clocks_in_memory).
- Nothing can be demolished.
So the town can never make wood again.

FIX
The first House is free too. The rule is already written in SYSTEMS § The first of each producer is free and GAME_SPEC l.1125 (extra, uncommitted, committed with this fix).
- hub/town/town_rules.gd: only wood_cost's free-first check uses PRODUCERS. Rename it FREE_FIRST, since a House makes nothing, and add HOUSE.
- Fix the wood_cost doc comment.
- The rule reads the current buildings, so a town that is already stuck gets its next House free.

TESTS (tests/unit/test_town_builder.gd)
- New: three Lumbermills first spend all 40. The House preview costs 0 and the House places. The second House costs 10 and is refused at 0 wood.
- Update test_placing_spends_the_cost_exactly: a second House does the spending now.
- Update test_the_first_lumbermill_is_free: it now takes five Houses to spend 40.
- Update test_the_hub_builds_on_a_clicked_hex: the menu reads "House · 0 wood", and wood stays at 40 after the first House.

ACCEPTANCE
BUILT green. The save shape does not change, so this is not a risky boundary.

NON-GOALS
The Mine and the Farm join FREE_FIRST in their own slices (ig-6m2.3.1, ig-6m2.5).
close_reason: Fixed by the director, committed 30c81eb (code) and 81d7909 (docs). The first House is free (TownRules.FREE_FIRST). New test: three Lumbermills first, then a free House, then wood flows. BUILT green: gate 0/0, GUT 673/673.

title: Living-world 2, slice 1: one dream, one bond, one moment
description:
WHY
The living-world direction bets that heroes become people worth knowing. Before food, walking, meals and gossip are built (the full ig-m6o.2 scope), this slice tests that bet on what exists today: the Ledger's battle, rescue and death records, the town with its embodied hero, and the hero detail panel. One bond, one dream, one moment in town. The owner plays it, and the full scope starts only if the feeling lands.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction (owner, 2026-09-24). DECISIONS.md 2026-09-24 "The Ledger" (item 5 for record shapes; item 9 and "Rejected: saved tallies" for derived readers). ARCHITECTURE.md "Ambient heroes are views onto the roster". SYSTEMS.md § Bonds and dreams, slice 1.
No saved state. The bond and the dream are derived from the Ledger when read, like the History list, so nothing crosses save boundary #1 and no ADR is needed.

BEHAVIOR
1. Bond points: a pure static reader under history/ (the Ledger pattern). No GameSession field, and no cache that outlives one read. For two living heroes A and B, add up the facts below. Each fact counts at most once per record for a pair.
   - A hard battle together: a battle record with both in team that is not routine (Ledger.is_routine). Routine victories count nothing.
   - One saved the other in battle: a revived or carried moment between them, either way round.
   - One rescued the other: a rescue battle record with one in rescuers and the other in rescued. A record without rescuers gives no rescue points (legacy; it reads neutrally, as in the History list).
   - A death witnessed together: both in the team of the battle record whose order equals a died record's battle_order, and neither is the dead hero.
   Points and the threshold are balance.tres rows (SYSTEMS § Bonds and dreams, all PROVISIONAL).
2. A hero's bond is the living roster hero with the most points, if at or over the threshold. Ties go to the more recent last shared fact (higher seq), then instance_id. One bond per hero; A's closest may have someone else as their own closest.
3. The dream is "repay a life debt". Any hero can hold it; it is the one kind of dream in this slice. It is derived from the hero's records, oldest first:
   - A save opens a debt when none is open: this hero is in rescued on a rescue record with rescuers (owed to the first id listed), or a revived or carried moment names this hero, with a hero id as by.
   - The debt is paid when this hero saves the one it owes (the same two facts, reversed).
   - The debt is lost when the one it owes has a died record.
   - After it is paid or lost, the next save opens a new debt.
4. The hero detail panel shows both, for the selected hero only, above History. Not in the roster tooltip: that would read the Ledger once per row.
   - "Closest to Mara: 4 hard fights, 1 rescue, 1 death seen together." Shown only at or over the threshold, with " (away)" while Mara is busy.
   - "Dream: repay Mara." with three milestones, each marked done or not done: "Mara carried Dunn out at Ashen Road." (the save that opened it), "Fight beside Mara again (1/3).", "Save Mara."
   - After it ends, until the next debt: "Dream fulfilled: repaid Mara at Ashen Road." or "Dream lost: Mara died before the debt was paid."
   - No debt yet: no Dream line.
5. The moment in town. While the player walks hero A, A's bonded partner B stands in town if B is not busy (is_hero_busy): at B's house if B has one, else near the spawn point. B idles: no walking, no pathing. When A comes within the meeting distance, B turns to face A, plays the existing Interact clip once, and a line shows above B for a few seconds. The line comes from their strongest shared fact (most points; ties go to the most recent) and names a real place or person from the Ledger:
   - B saved or rescued A: "I'd come for you again. Ashen Road or anywhere."
   - A saved or rescued B: "I haven't forgotten Ashen Road. I owe you."
   - A death seen together: "I still think about Aldo."
   - Hard fights only: "Four hard fights, and we're both still standing."
   It plays once per approach and re-arms when A walks away. The figure is a view onto the roster: hub.gd hands TownView the partner and the line, TownView never reads GameSession, and it refreshes on roster_changed and expeditions_changed. Presentation numbers (meeting distance, line time, spawn offset) stay in the view script.

ACCEPTANCE
- GUT, bond reader: each fact type scores alone; a routine victory scores 0; a pair at the threshold bonds and one point short does not; a dead hero is never a bond; the tie-break is stable; a record without rescuers, or a died record without battle_order, scores no rescue or witness points and raises no error.
- GUT, dream: a save opens a debt; shared battles advance milestone 2; the reverse save pays it; the owed hero's death loses it; the next save opens a new debt.
- No saved state. Grep: the diff adds no to_dict or from_dict key, no SaveService change and no GameSession field (boundary #1 untouched).
- Read cost: measure one bond and dream read for one hero at the 10,000-record cap (best of seven, the test_ledger.gd style) and print it for this bead. It is a measurement for ig-m6o.2.2's derived-or-stored ADR, not a gate. Hard rule: the read runs on refresh only, never per frame.
- Town, headless test: embody A with a bonded, idle B. B's figure exists. Moving A inside the distance plays the greeting and shows the line once; moving away and back shows it again. Sending B on an order removes the figure. A hero with no bond adds no figure.
- Calibration: copy the owner's save first, then run the reader over the copy: ledger.jsonl, or the embedded "ledger" key in save.json if the save predates ig-m6o.9. Report how many bonds and debts it yields. Never open the owner's folder for writing, and never run Godot against the owner's real APPDATA. Screenshots of the detail panel and the meeting go in .agent-results/<this id>/.
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass mandatory (boundary #2: the town figure and the hub wiring; plus a read-only check that nothing new is saved).
- Owner gate, last. The owner plays a normal session with the slice. If no bond has formed after about an hour, the builder supplies a seeded save in a throwaway APPDATA, never the owner's real save. The owner judges one thing: is the partner someone worth knowing? Yes: the full ig-m6o.2 scope starts, after ig-6m2.5.1 and ig-6m2.6 (both slices). No: record what fell flat on ig-m6o.2, and the full scope does not start.

NOTE
- The town today shows only the embodied hero; nobody wanders yet (that is ig-6m2.6.2). This slice adds exactly one standing figure. When ig-6m2.6.2 lands, B's figure becomes B's ambient hero, not a second copy.
- Routine victories are the first records the Ledger evicts, which is also why they score nothing: a bond built on them would fade at the cap. Other records can still be evicted at the 10,000 cap, so an old bond can weaken. Known ceiling.
- Touches hub/hub.gd (detail panel) and hub/town/. Build after ig-gy0.3, which also touches hub.gd, and never run beside it.

NON-GOALS
Gossip; testimony (architecture note 9); meals and food (ig-6m2.5); walking, wandering and pathing (ig-6m2.6); more than one bond shown per hero; directed or layered relationships; bond decay; any saved bond or dream state, and so any ADR; a notice when a bond forms; any effect of bonds on combat or stats; new animation clips or downloads; profession dreams.

title: Ledger save shape: append-only side file, so a save never rewrites history
description:
WHY
Measured in ig-m6o.1's acceptance (.agent-results/ig-m6o.1/gut_ledger2.log): at the 10,000-record cap, a real save takes 108 ms, a load takes 197 ms, and the file is 3,876,169 bytes (about 390 bytes a record, tab-indented).
Every profile action (_commit_profile_mutation) and every 15 s periodic save while expeditions run rewrites the whole ledger. So the hitch grows about 11 us per record, forever.
It reaches one 60 FPS frame (16.7 ms) at about 1,500 records. At a desk guess of 60 records an hour, that is about 25 hours of play.
That breaks the 60 FPS hard constraint. Lowering the cap would hide it by throwing away the history the direction exists to keep.
Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § The Ledger (the save budget row).

DESIGN RULE (game-designer, 2026-09-24)
A save's cost must not grow with history. The ledger adds at most 2 ms to any save or profile action, at any size up to the cap. The cap stays 10,000.

PROPOSED SHAPE (godot-architect amends the ADR; the director accepts it before code)
- The records move to an append-only JSON Lines side file (one record per line, not indented, still human-readable). Suggested path: user://ledger.jsonl.
- A commit appends only the new records and flushes, then writes the main save as today.
- The main save keeps `ledger_next_seq` as the high-water mark. On load, lines with seq >= that mark are dropped: they were appended, but the main save never landed. So a snapshot never holds history the main save does not know about. This keeps ADR item 4 ("never one without the other") with a mark instead of one file.
- If the append fails, the mutation fails and rolls back, as a failed save does today.
- An orphan line must never collide with a later seq. The implementer either truncates the file back to its old length, or keeps seq advanced (a gap is allowed; reuse is not).
- The rollback snapshot in _commit_profile_mutation leaves the records out. Rolling back is a truncate to the old length, not a deep copy of 10,000 dicts.
- Eviction runs in memory, and only AFTER the mutation commits (director edge, 2026-09-24). An append into a full ledger that then fails would otherwise have evicted a record that truncating cannot bring back. Evicting after commit needs no extra rollback state. The in-memory list sits above the cap only for the length of one mutation.
- The file is compacted (rewritten to the capped list) only at load, behind the load, never mid-play.
- Migration: a save that still embeds `ledger` moves it to the file once on load and stops writing the key. A missing or unreadable side file loads as an empty ledger with a push_warning. Readers already tolerate gaps.
- This amends the ADR's Rejected line "a separate save file". The high-water mark is the reason it is safe now.

REJECTED
- A lower cap: about 1,500 records to fit one frame. That throws away the history Nemesis, graves and the Chronicle read.
- Keeping one file but writing it compact and skipping the rollback deep copy: roughly halves the cost. It is still O(history) on every click, and still over one frame at the cap.
- A save thread: the snapshot is still built on the main thread, and it adds concurrency to the save boundary.

ACCEPTANCE
- Timed saves at 0 and at 10,000 records differ by at most 2 ms (godot-tester), including a profile action (_commit_profile_mutation) and a periodic save.
- A real disk round-trip keeps every record and ledger_next_seq.
- Crash cases, each through a real disk reload:
  - The append lands and the main save fails: the orphan lines are dropped, and the next seq does not collide.
  - The side file is missing: the ledger loads empty and the game plays on.
- A legacy save with an embedded `ledger` migrates to the file once, with no record lost or duplicated.
- Load-time compaction applies the tiered eviction exactly.
- Rollback at the cap: a mutation that appends to a ledger of exactly 10,000 records and then fails leaves the in-memory ledger equal to the pre-mutation one (nothing evicted, nothing appended). After a real disk reload, the loaded ledger equals it too.
- BUILT + GUT green. Sol review: boundary #1 (a second save file).

SEQUENCING
- Not urgent: a fresh save has no records, and the hitch builds up slowly.
- Land it before the owner's long playtests, and before ig-m6o.2 raises the record rate (meals, encounters). It blocks ig-m6o.2.
notes:
DIRECTOR 2026-09-24: ADR amendment accepted (DECISIONS Ledger items 1, 8 and Rejected; ARCHITECTURE autoload table names ledger.jsonl). Two crash rules added to acceptance: (1) load-time compaction writes a temp file then renames it over ledger.jsonl, the way SaveService replaces save.json; an interrupted compaction leaves the old file whole. (2) A torn last line (crash mid-append) is dropped at load; its main save never landed. Test both through a real disk reload.
2026-09-24 impl done, uncommitted. Side file user://ledger.jsonl via SaveService (append+flush before main save, resize-undo on main-save failure, load drops seq>=mark / torn / bad lines, load-time compaction temp+rename, legacy embedded ledger migrates once). GameSession: eviction held until commit succeeds (_ledger_hold_depth), rollback truncates in place, _ledger_tiers parallel array so Ledger.evict is a native find. BUILT green: gate exit 0; GUT 568/568. Cap (10k): save before 106/104/117 ms -> commit 0.87-1.16 ms, periodic save 3.3-4.0 ms (main save itself, empty-ledger baseline ~3 ms), first unsynced save 77 ms once. Load before 201 ms -> ~300 ms in GUT (includes load-time compaction rewrite + existing parse/normalize). Budget test medians: commit +<=1 ms, periodic +<=0.3 ms vs empty. Sol (high) FAIL on 5 points: #1 rewrite+main-fail window (only for a foreign ledger; production never does that - covered the real path with a new reload test), #2 summon/rank-up/kill ignore save failures (pre-existing, outside seams), #3 recovery rewrite in save() over budget (recovery only), #4 weak append test (fixed), #5 no warning for missing side file at mark 1 (doc question). Evidence .agent-results/ig-m6o.9/, Sol log .agent-results/logs/ig-m6o.9-sol.json.
Director rulings on Sol's FAIL (2026-09-24):
- Point 3, the ~77 ms recovery rewrite: accepted. from_dict runs only in load_game and the two rollbacks, and a rollback restores the same list object, so steady play always appends. DECISIONS item 8 and the SYSTEMS budget row now exempt it, the same as load compaction.
- Point 5, a missing file at mark 1 loads silently: the code is right. DECISIONS item 1 is amended to match.
- Point 2, roster saves ignore a failed save: this predates m6o.9 and is filed as ig-8hj.
- An unreadable side file must block the load, like an unreadable main save. Loading empty let compaction overwrite the real history. High1 is changing the code; DECISIONS item 1 is amended.
- Load cost far over the cap (~0.3 ms per evicted record): get a ponytail comment on Ledger.evict.
- The budget test (median of 7 against a 2 ms bar, ~1 ms measured) stays as is.
2026-09-24 director rulings applied: pts 3/5 accepted (docs amended by director), pt 2 filed separately. Code: an existing side file that won't open now blocks the load before from_dict/compaction (save_service load_game + _read_ledger_file 'error' key); no test, since Godot on Windows can't make an existing unopenable file from GDScript (a dir reads as missing; a held handle doesn't lock). ponytail comment on Ledger.evict. BUILT green: gate 0, GUT 568/568, Godot 0.
close_reason: Done. Code 5a7b310, docs 7cd15d1. The records live in user://ledger.jsonl; the main save keeps the mark. At the 10,000 cap a commit went from about 106 ms to about 0.9 ms. The ledger adds at most 0.7 ms per commit and 0.2 ms per periodic save. Sol's FAIL: points 1 and 4 fixed; 3 and 5 accepted with DECISIONS amendments; point 2 filed as ig-8hj. The unreadable-file wipe found in review now blocks the load. Director BUILT: gate exit 0, GUT 568/568, Godot reaped to 0.

title: Living-world 1: The Ledger, an append-only record of who did what to whom
description:
WHY
"The game remembers what we did." Every later system reads history: Nemesis, the Guest, the Chronicle, graves, the Parliament and Risen promotion. So the record has to exist before them. A fact that is never recorded can never be told later.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction, step 1. ADR: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-24 "The Ledger" (ACCEPTED 2026-09-24, with three director amendments: `team`, `battle_seq`, tiered eviction).
Sequencing (director): after ig-4if, before ig-gy0.2 (dep added).
Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § The Ledger (PROVISIONAL).

WHAT IT IS
- An append-only list of settled events: who did what to whom, when and where.
- History readers derive their accounts from it. Combat still resolves combat: combat/ never reads or writes the Ledger.
- Records are never edited. Only the size cap removes them.

WHERE IT LIVES (save boundary #1)
- Two additive GameSession keys: `ledger` (an Array of Dictionary) and `ledger_next_seq` (an int, starting at 1, never reused).
- SAVE_VERSION is not bumped (the P2-23 precedent). A save without the keys loads an empty ledger.
- Nothing is backfilled. Inventing history for old heroes would be a lie.

RECORD SHAPE
{"seq": int, "time": int (unix seconds at settle), "kind": String, ...fields}
- Heroes are named by instance_id. Enemies have no identity yet, so they appear as "enemy:<archetype>" plus the zone. The nemesis step gives them one.
- Only `summoned` and `died` store the hero's name. Readers resolve other ids through the roster or those two records.

v1 KINDS AND THEIR ONE WRITER EACH
1. `summoned` {hero, name, rank, archetype}. Writer: summon_hero.
2. `battle` {order, zone, battle_kind, result, team[], kills{hero: n}, moments[], rescued[]}. Writers: _settle_battle_order and _settle_rescue_order. One record per settled battle.
   - A moment is {tick, what: downed | revived | carried, hero, by}. `by` is a hero id or "enemy:<archetype>".
   - `team` holds the instance_id of every hero who fought, downed or not. It is the battle's witness list: a later per-hero-knowledge reader ("a hero knows what they saw") needs no backfill. (Director amendment.)
   - `rescued` holds the stranded heroes a rescue battle brought home. It is set only on rescue battles.
3. `died` {hero, name, rank, cause: expedition | sacrifice | starvation, zone?, by?}. Writer: kill_hero ONLY. It gains optional `cause` and `by` arguments.
   - A sacrifice passes cause sacrifice, and `by` is the keeper that took the Essence.
   - This keeps permadeath's one writer (boundary #3): the record of a death is written where the death happens.
   - An `expedition` death carries `battle_seq`, the seq of the battle that stranded the hero. (Director amendment.) Most of these deaths happen LATER than that battle: abandon_stranded, rescue-window expiry (_expire_stranded_incidents_in_memory), or a rescue that fails for some heroes (_settle_rescue_order). All three go through Expedition.finalize_permanent_losses. So:
     - _capture_stranded_incident stores the stranding battle's seq on the incident as the additive key `battle_seq` (boundary #1). The battle record is appended first, so its seq is known.
     - finalize_permanent_losses hands it to kill_hero(..., cause expedition), and the died record copies it.
     - An incident saved before this lands has no `battle_seq`, and neither does its died record. Readers tolerate that.
     - For a death after a failed rescue, `battle_seq` still points at the ORIGINAL stranding battle. The rescue battle's own record lists the rescuers in its `team`.
4. `ranked_up` {hero, from, to, via: "essence"}. Writer: rank_up_hero. Step 4 adds via "deeds".
5. `meal`: reserved and not written in v1. Step 2 writes it as a social event (who ate together, and where). Eating ticks are not events: they would flood the log and are not deeds.

NOT RECORDED IN v1
- per-hit or per-kill records (kills are a count per battle)
- forecasts, repeat-safety forecasts, previews and the arena prototype
- gear, XP and levels, homes, stations and building placement

THE BATTLE SIDE (touches the sim lightly)
- BattleState collects moments as they happen: the sim appends one when a hero is downed, revived (Rally or a draught) or carried out.
- Moments are saved with an in-flight battle as the additive BattleState key `moments`, so a mid-fight save and reload keeps them (boundary #1).
- BattleOutcome copies them. GameSession writes them into the battle record at settle.
- Moments are pure bookkeeping. They draw no RNG and change no combat result.
- The legacy_v2 backend reports none. Its battle record has empty moments.
- Heads-up for ig-gy0.1's golden digests: they hash every tick's state dict, so a new `moments` key changes them. Re-baseline, or leave `moments` out of the digest, and say which in the notes.

SIZE (SYSTEMS § The Ledger, PROVISIONAL)
- ledger_max_records 10000 and battle_max_moments 64. Past 64, drop the extras and set "moments_truncated": true.
- Over the record cap, eviction is tiered (director amendment), oldest first within a tier: (1) routine battles, meaning a victory `battle` with no moments and no rescued; (2) other `battle` records; (3) `ranked_up`; (4) `summoned`; (5) `died`, last of all.
- Readers must tolerate gaps. A hero with no `summoned` record "arrived before the records begin". This covers both legacy saves and eviction.

RULES CODE
- Pure static functions in one script, following ExpeditionOrders: append with cap and eviction, records for a hero, and history lines.
- GameSession mutators call it. Folder: tech-lead's call (suggestion: a new feature folder `history/`).
- No fourth autoload.

FIRST VISIBLE READER
- Hero detail (%HeroDetail in hub.gd) gains a short History list, newest first, at most 10 lines. The roster-list tooltip, which reuses _hero_detail_text, stays short. Examples:
  "Summoned at F rank." / "Downed by an enemy Rogue at Verdant; revived by Aldric." / "Won 12 battles at Verdant." (routine victories at one zone collapse into one line) / "Arrived before the records begin."
- Dead heroes leave the roster, so their history has no reader yet. Graves (step 6) is the first.

NATURAL SPLIT (if tech-lead wants two slices)
(a) The GameSession side: summoned, died, ranked_up, battle records from the outcome's existing fields, and the hero-detail reader.
(b) The sim moments, with killer and rescuer attribution. (a) can land while the sim is busy.

CROSS-LANE
- ig-6m2.5 (starvation) calls kill_hero. If the Ledger has landed, it passes cause starvation. If 6m2.5 lands first, the Ledger adds it.

ACCEPTANCE
- A real disk save and reload keeps `ledger` and `ledger_next_seq` byte-identical.
- A legacy save without either key loads, and its heroes show "Arrived before the records begin."
- An in-flight battle saved and reloaded mid-fight keeps its moments. Settling it writes exactly one battle record, with the right killer and rescuer ids.
- Each writer writes exactly one record per event:
  - a summon
  - a sacrifice (one `died`, cause sacrifice, by = the keeper; no second record)
  - a rank-up
  - an expedition death
  - a stranded-incident rescue (`rescued` filled)
- A forecast and a repeat-safety forecast leave the ledger unchanged.
- Filling past the cap evicts in tier order (routine battles, other battles, ranked_up, summoned, died). seq stays strictly increasing and is never reused.
- Every battle record's `team` equals the heroes who fought (downed ones included).
- An expedition death reached by abandon, by expiry and by a partly failed rescue each carries the stranding battle's `battle_seq`, and so does an incident that survives a real disk save and reload in between.
- kill_hero is still the only roster remover, and `died` is written nowhere else.
- Hero detail shows the history.

title: Direction: living-world
description:
WHY
The owner approved a new game direction on 2026-09-24, after an 8-round debate (director vs GPT-6 Astra). Direction v2 replaced it the same day, after a second 10-round debate. v2 is final.
Pitch: a living-world squad RPG where every summon brings someone worth knowing, every battle changes their relationships, and the town you build can rise to rescue them.
Spine: summon a person -> give them a home -> discover whom they love and what they want -> fight together -> let their choices, achievements and losses change the world.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction (owner, 2026-09-24): v2 sections 1-14, the design principles, § 13's owner rulings and § Kept in full. Everything the final compressed stays in force; only § 12 cuts.
ADR: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-24 "The Ledger" (ACCEPTED 2026-09-24 with three director amendments).

STANDING RULINGS (GAME_SPEC § Direction § 11; 1-5 keep their v1 numbers)
1. Old World yes: succession preserves independent worlds beyond player ownership. Amends one-roster-forever (GAME_SPEC § Win and loss).
2. Power from both paths: deeds and sacrifice both fund advancement; their histories produce different testimony. Rank-ups spend Essence.
3. Defiance yes: reasoned refusals, living departures and earned overthrow change the campaign.
4. Dead never playable: no soul state returns to Alive; spectral effects act through current vessels. kill_hero() stays the only way a hero dies.
5. Only Risen take the chair: born F, reached SSS, a personal ascent deed before every promotion (director call, standing).
6. One soul, one presence: visits and transfers vacate prior active roles; dream projections are views of the same living actor.
7. Live-time only: hunger, memory, travel, seasons and old worlds freeze when closed, without catch-up. One exception (owner ruling 2026-09-24): timed sent expeditions still finish while closed and resolve once on reopening (ig-6l4). Everything else freezes.
Design principle, not a ruling: Personhood persists. The Door carries accountability to sacrificed souls, not automatic custody of them.

OWNER RULINGS (§ 13; owner, 2026-09-24, "A all")
- Miracle-born person: a genuinely new mortal person, not a construct. New identity, no invented past; rare and costly (numbers: game designer). (ig-m6o.5)
- A former town summons the Door: a covenant arrival, binding only if the player or their Herald agreed to it earlier; otherwise an invitation the player can decline. (ig-m6o.8)
- Concordance between worlds: one coupled formation, not separate walking cities; every community keeps its agency. (ig-m6o.8)
- Expeditions while the game is closed: keep the ig-6l4 exception (ruling 7).

BUILD ORDER
The eight children are wired in order. Each one lands one new feeling. tech-lead splits each step into slices when its turn comes. Nothing is built toward a later step ahead of time: no scaffolding and no "we'll need it" fields.
1. Ledger
2. People at home
3. People in combat
4. Summoning with consequences
5. Institutions
6. Death and power
7. Fate
8. Spectacle and Old World
v2's list for each step, the Appendix A2 mechanics, the three § 14 twists and the director's architecture notes (v2 Appendix B) are notes on the step beads. A twist gets a scoped bead only when its step is next.
ADR BLOCKERS (label needs-adr; godot-architect writes them before the step builds): .5 (notes 2 and 7: living roster exits and new roster entries), .6 (note 8: the soul registry), .7 (nemesis identity, from its body), .8 (note 10: world files).

SEQUENCING (accepted by the director, 2026-09-24)
- The skills lane (ig-gy0) and the town lane (ig-6m2, ig-wgj.10-.12) keep going.
- Step 1 comes after ig-4if and before ig-gy0.2 (dep added).
  - Nemesis, the Guest and the Chronicle all read it, so every later record it misses is lost for good.
  - It touches battle_simulation.gd lightly, and waiting for gy0.1's refactor to settle avoids a collision.
- Step 2 waits on the town food and walking slices. Step 3 waits on the skills epic.

SPINE FLAG
Living Essence (steps 4-5) adds a second Essence source next to sacrifice, and its formulas are undecided. It moves the ~327-pull spine and the "manufacture, don't pray" claim (SYSTEMS.md § Sacrifice -> rank up, GAME_SPEC § Win and loss). No Essence formula ships until game-designer restates the spine with both sources.

CUT, MERGED AND RESTORED (GAME_SPEC § Direction § 12)
- Cut: duplicate souls and alternate selves (distinct associates instead); permanent F-rank invisibility (earned recognition instead); universal ascension and compulsory retirement death (Founding and living aftermath instead).
- Merged: diaries, enemy chronicles and performances share authored-account machinery; chorus arrivals feed Guest collisions; stolen names and hollows can combine but stay distinct.
- Restored: promises reshape geography; musical motifs enable real counters; shared dream-spaces are explorable.
- Spine test: every activity must change a particular person, relationship, institution or inherited obligation.
notes: 2026-09-24 owner ruling ('A all'), the 4 Direction v2 decisions: (1) The Person Nobody Summoned = A, a real new person, rare and costly. (2) A former apprentice's town summons the Door = A, binding only if the player or their Herald agreed earlier; otherwise an invitation the player can decline. (3) Concordance between worlds = A, one coupled formation. (4) Expeditions while the game is closed = A, keep the ig-6l4 exception. extra folds these into the docs with B and C; decision 4 settles the offline PROVISIONAL; D stays PROVISIONAL.

title: Skills 5: the AI answers enemy telegraphs (stun, interrupt, shield, dodge); enemies get skills
description:
WHY
The owner: "the heros AI should be able correctly respond to enemie skills too. As in enemie telegraphed heavy attack/skill -> hero uses available stun skill etc etc".
Spec: SYSTEMS.md § Skills (Counters, The AI's answer, Enemies). DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Skills" items 7, 8.

BEHAVIOR
1. Counter tags on the v1 counters (stun, interrupt, shield, dodge), including Rally (shield), Flank/Interrupt (interrupt) and the general Brace (shield), Tumble (dodge) and Disrupt (interrupt).
2. Picker priority gains "counter" at the top.
3. The answer: once an enemy telegraph has run skill_reaction_delay_seconds, heroes in stable spawn order may claim it. Stun or interrupt the caster in range first; else shield someone inside it; else dodge if inside it; else walk out (today's evade). Shortest cooldown first. One claim per telegraph, saved on the telegraphing actor as telegraph_claimed_by. Manual and off skills are never used as counters.
4. Enemy kits (owner ruling 2026-09-23: enemies get skills): enemies gain their class's starter weaponskill; enemy Knights gain Crushing Blow (1.2 s telegraph, radius 1.5 on its target, 2.5x, 14 s). Enemies use the picker without chains or counters.
5. The view shows who answered (a small callout on the answering hero). Nothing else new in the view.

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests: a Knight with Buckler Blow in range stuns a Crushing Blow and the telegraph never resolves; two heroes with stuns spend only one; with no stun in range, a shield lands on the target; a Rogue inside the circle uses Slip and takes no damage; after the reaction delay, not before; a manual counter is never auto-fired.
- A hero with both a class counter and a general counter ready uses the class one (shortest cooldown).
- A save mid-telegraph after a claim reloads without a second answer (boundary #1).
- Forecast within 2x the ig-gy0.1 baseline.
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass (boundary #4).

NON-GOALS
Chains (ig-gy0.5); balance (ig-gy0.9); enemies using the general pool (they never do).

BUILT green: gate exit 0 zero errors/warnings; GUT 608/608 (.agent-results/ig-gy0.4/gate2.log, gut2.log). Forecast (5 runs, ms, golden_capture.gd copy): verdant5 median 436 vs 311 (1.40x); frontier50 median 9336 vs 8203 (1.14x); within 2x (timing.log). Pre-skills checkpoint golden: re-recorded per director ruling (option 1) via .agent-results/ig-gy0.4/regen_pre_skills_expected.gd; old copy pre_skills.expected.before.json. Proof: with _answer_telegraphs and the enemy_kit spawn switched off, the old build's outcome matched exactly and the final state differed only by the new telegraph_claimed_by key (.agent-results/ig-gy0.4/experiment_off.log); _pre_skills_shape now strips telegraph_claimed_by and last_counter_tick. QuickResolve: skill-blind by ADR item 2; nothing needed, Wave unchanged. Late telegraph tick (1.2 s lands 1.3 s) is ig-85w, left alone.
2026-09-24 review: fixed the dodge tier to match SYSTEMS (every hero inside with a dodge uses it; the first holds the claim) + test. Sol (gpt-6-sol high, read-only, no Godot) PASS WITH NITS; #1 holds for game-produced saves, #4 holds (QuickResolve legacy_v2 skill-blind, Wave.from_zone unchanged). Log .agent-results/logs/ig-gy04-sol.json. Nit 1 fixed: enemies no longer accept the general pool (BattleActor.kit_archetypes). Nit 2 (any non-empty claim string accepted; a hand-edited claim would suppress answers) and nit 3 (claim test writes the profile to disk directly, not via SaveService.save, same as the file's _through_disk helper) left as is. Final BUILT: gate exit 0, zero errors/warnings (gate4.log); GUT 609/609 (gut4.log).
close_reason: Heroes answer enemy telegraphs after skill_reaction_delay_seconds (stun or interrupt, else shield, else every hero inside dodges; one claim, saved on the caster). Enemies get their level-1 class skills; enemy Knights get Crushing Blow. The pre-skills golden was re-baselined by director ruling (option 1), proven by the switched-off run. Director BUILT: gate exit 0, GUT 609/609 (15842 asserts), reap 0. Sol PASS WITH NITS (#1 and #4 hold); nits 2 and 3 accepted. Follow-ups: the dodge zero-margin finding is on ig-gy0.9, and the late tick is ig-85w. Commit 39969c7.

title: Skills 4: heroes learn by level; bar order and modes saved on the hero; skill panel
description:
WHY
The owner wants a customizable skill bar per hero. This slice saves a hero's bar (order and modes) and shows it. Level skills stay derived.
Spec: DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Skills" items 3 and 4. GAME_SPEC.md § Skills ("The bar", "Learning").

BEHAVIOR
1. Hero additive keys: learned_skills (empty until ig-gy0.7), skill_bar [{id, mode}], skill_chains (empty until ig-gy0.5). Derived default bar when absent: every known skill, auto, kit order. Load validation drops unknown ids, other-class ids, unknown skills and bad modes with push_warning. A general id is valid on every class.
2. The dispatch team snapshot carries skills (known skills in bar order, with modes) and chains. Fixed at dispatch, like gear.

- A hero who levels past 5 gains the level-5 skills in its bar without a save change, appended in kit order.
- A skill set to manual is never auto-fired; off is never fired.

Touches heroes/hero.gd and GameSession save keys, like ig-wgj.13 and ig-6m2.1. Never run beside them.

Books and teaching (ig-gy0.7); chains UI (ig-gy0.5); pilot hotbar (ig-gy0.6).

title: Skills 1: skills become data (the four signatures and passives run by skill id), no behavior change
description:
WHY
The skill system needs every skill to be data that one generic function applies. Today the four signatures are hard-coded: BattleSimulation.ABILITIES is keyed by archetype, _use_ability does `match actor.archetype`, _auto_ability_wanted is per-archetype code, and HeroDefinition.battle_ability duplicates the dict. This slice moves them to data with NO behavior change, so every later slice adds skills as .tres files.
Spec: DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Skills" items 1, 2, 4, 5. SYSTEMS.md § Skills.

BEHAVIOR
1. AbilityDefinition grows the fields in the ADR item 1: skill_id, kind, archetype, unlock_level, book_only, counter_tag, combo_after, the AI rule fields, effects (a list of primitive dicts or sub-resources: the implementer picks one, and keeps it one).
2. The four .tres files carry today's numbers as effects. The four passives become passive skills with today's numbers.
3. ABILITIES becomes a const dict keyed by skill id. HeroDefinition.battle_ability is removed; the archetype's default kit (passive + signature) is a lookup.
4. _use_ability applies effects through one function. No `match actor.archetype` left in skill code.
5. _auto_ability_wanted reads the skill's AI rule fields.
6. BattleActor: per-skill cooldowns ({skill_id: seconds}) replace ability_cooldown; the actor's skill list ([{id, mode}]) replaces ability_auto.
7. Old checkpoints load: ability_cooldown -> the signature's cooldown; the order's ability_auto policy -> the signature's mode. validate_snapshot accepts both shapes. New orders still write what they write today (ig-gy0.3 changes that).
8. The team snapshot may carry skills; without it the actor gets the archetype default (which is every snapshot in this slice).

ACCEPTANCE
- Golden: the ig-544 starter cases (five mixed F-rank, three Knights; seeds 1 and 2) produce identical BattleOutcome dicts before and after, tick for tick. Record them before touching code.
- A pre-change battle checkpoint saved to disk loads and finishes identically (boundary #1).
- A test loads every skill .tres and fails on an unknown primitive or field.
- Forecast baseline: wall time of BattleSimulation.forecast for a five-hero Verdant order and a 50-hero Frontier March order, recorded in the bead notes. Later slices are held to 2x this.
- grep: no `match actor.archetype` in skill application; no battle_ability anywhere.
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass mandatory (boundaries #1 and #4).

NON-GOALS
New skills; the Cleric (ig-4if); statuses; saving anything on Hero; any UI change.

NOTE
Wait for ig-hpu (in progress in combat/battle/*) to land first.

title: Skills 3: the v1 kits (40 skills, statuses, combos) and the one AI picker
description:
WHY
The owner wants heroes with many skills, picked intelligently by the AI. This slice adds all 40 v1 class skills, the 6 general-pool skills and the one generic picker. Heroes get them by level (derived from snapshot level + archetype), so every battle changes.
Spec: SYSTEMS.md § Skills (shared rules, statuses, the v1 kits). DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Skills" items 1, 5, 7.

BEHAVIOR
1. The remaining v1 skills as .tres: weaponskills, abilities, the Cleric's rest, class book skills, and the six general skills (archetype `general`, tiered; SYSTEMS.md § The v1 general pool). Book and general skills are usable if known; nothing grants them until ig-gy0.7.
2. Weaponskills ride the swing: fire in place of a basic attack, same windup, same interval reset. Combos: the step-2 bonus applies within skill_combo_window_seconds of step 1.
3. Abilities: own cooldown + skill_ability_lock_seconds after any ability. Signatures keep their numbers.
4. Statuses on BattleActor: a list with id, kind, source, remaining, magnitude. Stun, shield, damage reduction (strongest wins), stat changes (six stats only), bleed/burn/heal-over-time (tick every skill_status_tick_seconds), root, silence, taunt. guard_remaining/guard_reduction migrate to a damage-reduction status; old checkpoints convert on load.
5. The picker, one function, per actor when it can act: revive > heal > buff > attack (counters come in ig-gy0.4, chains in ig-gy0.5). Ties by the actor's skill order. Each skill's AI rule is data.
6. The actor's known skills = archetype kit skills with unlock_level <= snapshot level (plus any learned list in the snapshot, empty until ig-gy0.3).
7. Arcane Flow applies to every Mage ability.
8. VFX: one generic effect per primitive, tinted per skill. Our own glyphs if any icon is needed.

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests per primitive and per status (refresh not stack, strongest DR, shield before HP, DoT ticks).
- A 32-skill stress actor (test-only kit) runs a full battle.
- An actor knowing a full class kit plus all six general skills runs a full battle; on a fixed seed with no telegraphs, its damage dealt equals the class-only run (general skills add no damage).
- Forecast wall time within 2x the ig-gy0.1 baseline for the five-hero Verdant and 50-hero Frontier March orders.
- A mid-battle checkpoint with statuses round-trips to disk (boundary #1); a pre-ig-gy0.2 checkpoint loads.
- Record the new Verdant F-rank clear times (seeds 1, 2) in the notes for ig-gy0.9. Do not tune here.
- No skill name matches a Square Enix skill name.

title: Passions: two per hero out of eight professions; a saved calling becomes the first passion
description:
WHY
The owner, 2026-09-23: "I like the rimworld inspired multi passion idea." A hero now has two passions instead of one calling. Two out of eight keeps a Rites passion at 1 in 4 (it was 1 in 5), so the SS->SSS gate gets easier to meet, not harder. This lands before ig-wgj.10/.11/.12 because all three read is_profession_master or the XP rate, and they share heroes/hero.gd.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § Heroes staff the buildings ("Born: two passions"). Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Keepers and professions (Passions table, XP block). Boundaries: DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: The town builder", item 12 (PROPOSED until the director accepts it).

BEHAVIOR
1. A fixed list of eight professions: smithing, rites, drill, tracking, alchemy (today's order), then woodcutting, mining, farming. Hero.PROFESSIONS (profession -> hall id) stays the five halls, because station validation reads it. The three new ones have no building yet; the town builder maps them to Lumbermill, Mine and Farm.
2. Hero.passions: 2 different professions from the eight. Replaces Hero.calling.
3. The roll stays a stable hash of instance_id, with no summon RNG draw (seeded summons must not shift): first = ALL[posmod(id.hash(), 8)], second = the other seven [posmod((id + "#2").hash(), 7)]. New heroes get it at creation.
4. Migration in Hero.from_dict:
   - "calling" present, "passions" absent -> passions[0] = calling, passions[1] from the second hash over the other seven
   - neither present -> both from the hash
   - "passions" present -> used as is, after validation (2 distinct known ids; otherwise re-derive with a push_warning)
   to_dict writes "passions" and stops writing "calling".
5. is_profession_master: the profession is in hero.passions and skill >= profession_skill_cap.
6. add_profession_xp: x passion_xp_multiplier for either passion. Rename calling_xp_multiplier -> passion_xp_multiplier in balance_table.gd AND balance.tres in the same change (a row renamed in the script only falls back to its default silently).
7. Anything in the UI that shows the calling shows both passions.

ACCEPTANCE
- A real disk round-trip: a save written by today's build (with "calling") loads, keeps the calling as passions[0], writes "passions" and no "calling" on the next save, and reloads identically (boundary #1).
- Tests: two passions always distinct; the hash is stable across runs; legacy calling -> first passion; a new hero's roll draws nothing from the summon RNG (a seeded summon sequence is unchanged); master needs a passion AND skill 5; x4 XP in either passion, x1 otherwise; final stats identical whatever the passions.
- grep: no "calling" left in *.gd except the from_dict migration read.
- BUILT + GUT green. A verifier pass is mandatory (boundary #1).

NON-GOALS
Woodcutting/mining/farming XP or bonuses (the worker job-skills bead); any building for the new professions; changing the XP scale.
notes:
Implemented 2026-09-23 (not staged). hero.gd: ALL_PROFESSIONS (8, fixed order), passions: Array[StringName], passions_for(id) + _second_passion(id, first) per spec hashes; _read_professions migrates calling->passions[0], neither->hash, validates saved passions via _valid_passions (2 distinct known ids, else push_warning + fallback to calling/hash); to_dict writes passions, not calling. add_profession_xp/is_profession_master read passions. balance_table.gd + balance.tres renamed calling_xp_multiplier->passion_xp_multiplier together. hub.gd: detail shows 'Passions: A, B'; keeper row 'passion' / 'passions A, B'; picker ' · passion'. profession_xp validation left on the 5 halls (non-goal: no woodcutting XP yet; ig-6m2.7 must widen it). title: Skill system: learnable skills, AI that picks and counters, programmable chains, take control of one hero
description:
WHY
The owner, 2026-09-23:
"I want each hero to have customizable skill bar, I want them to be able to have 30+ skills if I wanted. We can bulk up the skills list by poaching skills from final fantasy 14, the mmo"
"I want AI to intelligently pick skills, but players can also take control basically play an mmo character. I think players should be able to program skill order too, as in theres one trigger skill and the player can choose what skills come after it. Also the heros AI should be able correctly respond to enemie skills too. As in enemie telegraphed heavy attack/skill -> hero uses available stun skill etc etc"
Owner rulings: learn from level/rank, skill books and the Training Hall; no bar limit, every learned skill usable.

SPEC
- Design: GAME_SPEC.md § Skills (under § Combat model)
- Numbers and the v1 kits (5 classes x 8): SYSTEMS.md § Skills (all PROVISIONAL)
- Boundaries: DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Skills are data the one simulation reads" (accepted 2026-09-23), ARCHITECTURE.md § Skills block
- FFXIV is inspiration only: our names, numbers, icons, effects. No Square Enix names or close copies.

SLICES (thin, in order; deps are in bd)
- ig-gy0.1 skills become data: the 4 signatures + passives run from AbilityDefinition by skill id. No behavior change. Forecast timing baseline.
- ig-4if the Cleric gets Mend + Grace (reused bead)
- ig-gy0.2 the v1 kits: all 40 class skills + the 6 general skills, statuses, combos, the generic AI picker
- ig-gy0.3 heroes learn by level; bar order and modes saved on the hero; the skill panel
- ig-gy0.4 the AI answers telegraphs; enemies get skills (Crushing Blow)
- ig-gy0.5 chains: a trigger and what follows, programmed by the player
- ig-gy0.6 take control of one hero, thin (click + number keys, watched battles)
- ig-gy0.7 skill books (class and general) and Training Hall teaching (class ahead of level, general by tier)
- ig-gy0.8 pilot v2: WASD, tab-target, camera follow, keybinds (later)
- ig-gy0.9 balance pass

OWNER RULINGS, 2026-09-23 (all four answered)
1. Class skills plus a shared general pool (6 in v1, tiered, books and Training Hall only, never by level, no damage). Not other classes' skills. This is the road to 30+.
2. Learned skills die with the hero (death and sacrifice).
3. Click + number keys first; WASD stays ig-gy0.8.
4. Enemies get skills.
Director: a Manual skill inside a programmed chain fires. Retiring legacy_v2 stays open in the ADR.

PARALLEL WITH THE TOWN BUILDER
- combat/battle/* slices (ig-gy0.1, ig-4if, ig-gy0.2, ig-gy0.4) share no files with the town lane. They can run beside ig-wgj.13 / ig-wgj.10 / ig-6m2.1 if only one of them runs the engine at a time.

title: Town builder 2: the seven halls become placed buildings you can move
description:
WHY
The owner wants the player to build their own town. After ig-6m2.1 the seven halls are still fixed nodes in town.tscn. This slice makes them placed buildings, like the rest, so the player can move them. It also gives each building type its own scene, which the paused visual beads (ig-wgj.6, ig-wgj.7) need.
Boundaries: DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: The town builder", item 3.

BEHAVIOR
1. Every building type gets its own scene: model, pick shape, label, and a work-spot marker (for keepers and workers to stand at later).
2. The halls join town_buildings, with their type name as id (Forge, Sanctum, and so on). They stay unique: place_building refuses a second one.
3. Default layout: a new profile, or a save without halls in town_buildings, gets the current authored positions snapped to hexes. building_levels is unchanged.
4. town.tscn loses its authored hall nodes. The town view spawns every building from town_buildings.
5. move_building(id, q, r): refuses a taken or off-map hex. Free in this slice (PROVISIONAL). Stations and homes keep their ids, so nothing is re-bound.
6. Click-to-open (ig-wgj.1) routes by building id exactly as today. The key 1-7 fallback still opens the seven halls.

ACCEPTANCE
- It survives save and reload: move the Forge, save to disk (APPDATA redirected), reload, and it is on the new hex with its level and keeper.
- An ig-6m2.1-era save loads with the default hall layout, and its placed buildings, homes and jobs are unchanged.
- Tests: a second hall is refused; a move to a taken hex is refused; after a move, the keeper, the level and every panel are unchanged; the key 1-7 fallback still works.
- Screenshots before and after a move, in .agent-results/<bead>/.
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green.
- A verifier pass is mandatory: boundaries #1 and #2 (this removes authored nodes that ig-wgj.1's click path and its tests read).

FILES
- hub/town/town.tscn, hub/town/town_view.gd, new per-type building scenes under hub/town/

- hub/hub.gd
- tests/unit/test_town_builder.gd, tests/unit/test_hub_controls.gd

NON-GOALS
level visuals (ig-wgj.6); keepers standing at work (ig-wgj.7); construction time (ig-6m2.3); a cost for moving; demolition.

title: Town builder 1: place a House and a Lumbermill on hexes, house a hero, put it to work, wood goes up
description:
WHY
The owner, 2026-09-23, wants a Banished-style town: the player places buildings, gives heroes houses and assigns work. This is the thinnest slice that proves the loop: place a House and a Lumbermill, house a hero, give it a job, and watch wood go up.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § The town builder. Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Town builder (all PROVISIONAL). Boundaries: DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: The town builder" (accepted 2026-09-23).

OWNER RULINGS (2026-09-23), what they mean for this slice
- A house is needed for a workplace job. Fighters, fodder and hall keepers need none (for now).
- Heroes eat and can starve. NOT in this slice: nobody eats until ig-6m2.5. Do not add food here.
- The new jobs are professions (woodcutting for the Lumbermill). NOT in this slice: woodcutting XP and the skill bonus land in the worker job-skills bead. Here a worker makes the flat wood_per_worker_minute.
- The town works only while you play (live tick only).

BEHAVIOR
1. Hex ground. A patch of hex_grass tiles, town_map_radius rings around the square. Stage hex_grass, building_home_A_blue and building_lumbermill_blue from the owner-approved KayKit Medieval Hexagon pack already on disk (C:\Users\Joony\AppData\Local\Temp\kaykit\town\). This is not a new download. Use the x3.0 scale from ig-wgj.3's notes. Measure the tile and record its size.
2. Hex math and rules live in one pure static script under hub/town/ (ExpeditionOrders precedent):
   - axial (q, r) to world position, and world position to the nearest hex
   - whether a hex is free: inside the map, not a hall's hex, not already built on
   - wood made in a tick
3. The seven halls stay authored nodes in hub/town/town.tscn. Their hexes count as taken (snap each hall's position to its hex).
4. GameSession gets:
   - town_buildings: a list of {id, type, q, r}; town_resources: {wood}; town_next_id
   - place_building(type, q, r): refuses a taken or off-map hex and a type it doesn't know, and refuses when wood is short. Spends the cost exactly. The id is "<type>_<n>".
   - assign_home(hero, house_id) and clear_home(hero). One hero per house (house_capacity).
   - station_hero(hero, building_id) accepts a placed Lumbermill id. It refuses a hero with no home, and a full workplace (lumbermill_worker_slots).
   - An exact preview for place_building (cost, and why it is refused).
5. Hero gets home: StringName, saved as the additive key "home". A missing key means no home.
6. Live tick only. In _advance_clocks_in_memory, each Lumbermill adds wood_per_worker_minute * delta / 60 for each worker who is home (not busy). _advance_orders_in_memory adds nothing.
7. Load cleanup. Extend ig-wgj.9's station cleanup: keep a workplace id only if the building exists and has a free slot. Clear a home whose house is gone or over capacity. First in roster order wins. push_warning for each clear.
8. UI:
   - the HUD shows wood
   - a Build button with House and Lumbermill. Click a free hex to place. A taken hex shows why it is refused.
   - clicking a House opens its panel: its resident, and Assign/Clear with the shared roster picker
   - clicking a Lumbermill opens its panel: its workers, "Away" for a busy one, the wood rate, and Assign/Unassign
   - the hero detail shows the hero's home and job
   - the dispatch preview lists workers too: "Lumbermill runs short while away (Mira)"

SAVE
Additive keys: town_buildings, town_resources, town_next_id on GameSession; home on Hero. Do not bump SAVE_VERSION. A save without town_resources gets town_start_wood once.

ACCEPTANCE
- It survives save and reload: place a House and a Lumbermill, house a hero, give it the job, let wood tick, save through SaveService to disk (APPDATA redirected), and reload. Buildings, home, job, wood and the partial unit all come back.
- A save from before this change loads with no placed buildings and town_start_wood.
- Tests:
  - placing on a taken hex, an off-map hex or a hall's hex is refused, and so is placing without the wood. A refusal spends nothing.
  - a hero with no home cannot take a Lumbermill job, and a full Lumbermill refuses a third worker
  - one hero per house
  - wood goes up on the live tick at the table rate, a busy worker adds 0, and an offline catch-up of any length adds 0
  - sacrifice refuses a worker, single and bulk (protected), and a worker can still be dispatched
  - after kill_hero() on a housed worker, the house and the workplace show a free slot, and no town code ran outside kill_hero
  - load cleanup: a job at a missing building, an over-full workplace, a home at a missing house
  - the preview equals the result
- A screenshot of the hex ground with a placed House and Lumbermill and wood above 0, in .agent-results/<bead>/.
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green.
- A verifier pass is mandatory: boundaries #1 (save), #2 (panels, town.tscn) and #3 (the death path must stay single-writer).

FILES
- heroes/hero.gd, systems/game_session.gd
- new: one pure rules script under hub/town/
- hub/town/town.tscn, hub/town/town_view.gd
- hub/hub.gd, hub/hub_ui_builder.gd
- balance_table.gd, balance.tres
- new models under hub/town/models/hexagon/ (hex_grass, building_home_A_blue, building_lumbermill_blue); add them to CREDITS.md's KayKit row

SEQUENCING
Starts after ig-wgj.9 lands: both edit station_hero, the station load cleanup, hero.gd and game_session.gd. Do not run it at the same time as ig-wgj.10, .11 or .12 (same files). Staging models runs the engine: serialize it.

NON-GOALS
moving or placing halls (ig-6m2.2); stone and construction time (ig-6m2.3); food; demolition; roads; heroes walking to work (ig-6m2.6); skills for the new job; anything while the game is closed.

title: Masterwork gates: Forge +13..+15 and the SS->SSS rank-up need a home master
description:
WHY

- SS->SSS needs a master priest (a Rites passion, skill 5) who is stationed at the Sanctum and home. The owner chose this knowingly, against the designer's and the director's advice.

description:

description:

title: Profession skills: calling, XP, masterwork check, and save round-trip
description:
WHY
Owner rulings, 2026-09-23:
- "I want the heroes themselves be the shopkeep NPCs, they have their own blacksmith skills, research skills, ect"
- "Born + practice. The calling is an immense xp boost, like the progression system in rim world. Also only the ones with calling can make masterwork(the final tier) equips/food/etc"
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § Heroes staff the buildings. Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Keepers and professions. Boundaries: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23, item 5.
The data comes first. Every staffing slice reads these fields, and they cross save boundary #1.

BEHAVIOR
1. Five profession ids, each mapped to the building id that ig-wgj.1 uses. Those ids are the node names in hub/town/town.tscn:
   - smithing -> &"Forge"
   - rites -> &"Sanctum"
   - drill -> &"TrainingHall"
   - tracking -> &"Reliquary"
   - alchemy -> &"Apothecary"
   Keep them in one const table on Hero, like STAT_NAMES.
2. New Hero fields:
   - calling: StringName
   - profession_xp: Dictionary[StringName, float], XP seconds per profession
3. Calling = the profession at index (instance_id.hash() mod 5), in profession-table order.
   - It is set at creation.
   - It is re-derived in from_dict when the save has no valid calling. from_dict overwrites instance_id, so derive after that.
   - No summon RNG draw is added.
4. Static helpers on Hero, following the SYSTEMS table:
   - profession_skill(hero, profession, balance) -> int: level k costs 20*k XP-minutes, capped at 5. The scale is the same for every hero and every profession.
   - add_profession_xp(hero, profession, work_seconds, balance): adds work_seconds * calling_xp_multiplier when profession == calling, otherwise work_seconds * 1.0. Nothing calls it yet; ig-wgj.10 wires it to the live tick.
   - is_profession_master(hero, profession, balance) -> bool: calling == profession and skill == 5.
5. New balance rows in balance_table.gd and balance.tres:
   - profession_xp_minutes_per_level (20.0)
   - profession_skill_cap (5)
   - calling_xp_multiplier (4.0)
6. Combat never reads these fields. compute_final_stats, hero_power and the forecast stay untouched.

SAVE
- Additive keys in Hero.to_dict/from_dict:
  - "calling": a String
  - "profession_xp": String -> float, with sorted keys so the output is stable
- A missing key gives the derived calling and no XP.
- An unknown profession id is dropped with push_warning.
- A negative or non-number XP value is reported with push_error and loads as 0. Match the existing validation style in from_dict.
- Do not bump SAVE_VERSION (P2-23 precedent).

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests:
  - The calling is stable for a given instance_id and is always one of the five.
  - Over 1000 new heroes, each profession gets 150-250.
  - profession_skill steps up at 20, 60, 120, 200 and 300 XP-minutes, and stays at 5 past that.
  - add_profession_xp with 60 s of work gives 240 XP-seconds in the calling and 60 in any other profession.
  - is_profession_master is true only for the calling at skill 5. A non-calling profession at skill 5 is not a master.
  - compute_final_stats is identical for two heroes that differ only in their profession fields.
  - The existing seeded summon tests pass unchanged.
- It survives save and reload:
  - to_dict -> from_dict keeps the calling and the XP.
  - A real disk round-trip through SaveService (APPDATA redirected) keeps them too.
  - An old save without the keys loads with derived callings and zero XP. After the next save and reload, the calling is the same one.
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green.
- Boundary #1 makes a verifier pass mandatory.

FILES

- balance_table.gd, balance.tres
- new: tests/unit/test_hero_professions.gd

NON-GOALS
stations; any UI; keeper bonuses; accruing XP on the tick; masterwork gates; a Circle keeper; research (parked for the base builder).

The calling is an immense xp boost, like the progression system in rim world. Also only the ones with calling can make masterwork(the final tier) equips/food/etc'. So: a calling is a RimWorld-passion-style large XP multiplier, and masterwork (the final tier) output is gated to calling heroes only. Q3 research is parked for the base builder.

title: Town builder: place buildings, house heroes, assign work (Banished-style layer)
description:
WHY
The owner, 2026-09-23: "It can be anyone. I intend any hero to be able to be able to run any shop pretty much. I also want the player to be able to build their own town, manage work, have the heros have their own house, city management like the game banished". The town builder is no longer parked. It is the direction.

SPEC
- Design: GAME_SPEC.md § The town builder, and § Heroes eat, and can starve to death
- Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Town builder (all PROVISIONAL)
- Boundaries: DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: The town builder" (accepted 2026-09-23; items 11 and 12 fold in the owner's answers), ARCHITECTURE.md § The town is the interface, and rule 8's amendment (accepted 2026-09-23)

OWNER RULINGS, 2026-09-23 (all four questions answered)
1. Houses: a house is needed for a workplace job. Fighters and fodder need none. Hall keepers need none for now.
2. Food: "They eat and can starve to death." Chosen against our recommendation, knowingly. Starvation goes through kill_hero(); a warning ladder makes every death visible; the death clock stops at a last warning until the player looks; only housed heroes who are home eat; nothing happens while the game is closed.
3. Job skills: "I like the rimworld inspired multi passion idea." Eight professions (the five halls plus woodcutting, mining, farming). Every hero has two passions. A Rites passion is 1 in 4 (was 1 in 5). A saved calling becomes the first passion.
4. Offline: live play only.

SLICES
- .1 place a House and a Lumbermill on hexes, house a hero, put it to work, wood goes up (thin first playable)
- .2 the seven halls become placed buildings you can move, and each building type gets its own scene
- .3 stone, and buildings that take time to go up
- .4 hall upgrades also cost wood and stone (changes today's costs)
- .5 food, farms and starvation (warned, never offline)
- .6 heroes walk home and to work (replaces ig-wgj.5, covers ig-wgj.7)
- worker job skills: woodcutting, mining and farming earn XP and a skill bonus (after .1, ig-wgj.10 and the passions bead)

PAUSED IN ig-wgj (fixed-layout work that would be thrown away)
- ig-wgj.5 ambient life: waits for .6, which replaces it
- ig-wgj.6 level visuals: waits for .3
- ig-wgj.7 keepers at work: waits for .2

STILL VALID
The passions bead, then ig-wgj.10 (keeper bonuses), .11 (masterwork draughts), .12 (masterwork gates). None of them reads the layout.

2026-09-23: the owner ruled that heroes are the shopkeepers (GAME_SPEC § Heroes staff the buildings). Keeper professions are the labor this economy would read: more slots per building means more keepers, and production scales with keeper skill. Non-roster workers still need a Scope-boundaries ruling. Also blocked by ig-wgj.10, so professions exist before the economy is designed.
2026-09-23 game-designer, town lane sweep. Settled in the docs and beads:
- Stone and construction numbers (ig-6m2.3). Wood-only building costs; stone pays only for hall upgrades.
- Hall upgrade wood and stone costs (ig-6m2.4). The parts cost stays.
- The first of each producer is free, a restart rule (ig-6m2.1 addendum, else .3).
- Draughts do not cost food (ig-6m2.5 item 9).
- Walking is cosmetic (ig-6m2.6).
- ig-wgj.6's new tier mapping.
Non-roster workers: settled. GAME_SPEC says "Nobody is hired. The town still has no NPCs": every worker is a roster hero.

title: Walk the town as your embodied hero (saved body, protected from spending)
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-23: "we see our heros walking around". GAME_SPEC § The town avatar (ruled 2026-08-13, pinned down 2026-09-23) says the player walks the town as one of their own roster heroes. title: Punchier squad battle hit and skill effects (first pass)
description:
Owner 2026-09-23: 'punchier effects for skills and attacks'. Now that units are KayKit models (ig-ixj), the existing effects (combat/battle/battle_vfx.gd: sparks _burst, _expanding_ring, _streak, crit label) read small and flat. First pass, polished later as we go. All values are PROVISIONAL feel numbers: put them as named constants at the top of battle_vfx.gd / battle_unit_view.gd so they can be tuned.

Build exactly these (director list, do not add others):
1. Hit flash: the struck model flashes white for ~0.08s on every landed hit, and stays brighter/longer on crit. Use ONE shared static overlay material (material_overlay) for the whole battle, not per-unit copies.
2. Camera shake: short trauma-style shake on crit and on every skill impact. Never on ordinary hits. It must follow the battle time scale and stop while paused. Put the camera offset on a child or on h_offset/v_offset so it doesn't fight the camera's own positioning in battle_view.gd.

title: [bug] Enemies face the wrong way when attacking in squad battle
description:
Owner report 2026-09-23 after ig-ixj: enemies face the wrong way when attacking. ig-ixj made the model yaw follow the sim facing exactly (atan2(fx, fy), facing_dot 1.00 in capture), so the model is now honest about whatever facing the sim holds. Diagnose first, with evidence: is it (a) stale sim facing while attacking, (b) skeleton models authored with the opposite forward axis to the hero models, or (c) something else. Check heroes too: owner named enemies, but confirm whether heroes attacking in place are also wrong.

Fix rules: attackers must visibly face their target during the attack. If the fix is in the sim (updating facing toward the target on attack), note that rogue flank (_is_behind, battle_simulation.gd:990) reads the TARGET's facing. Say in the report how the fix changes when flanks land, and add a test. If the fix is view-only, keep the sim untouched.

title: Squad battle units render as KayKit models with KayKit animations
description:
Squad battle units are still primitive capsules (combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd:_build_visual, :282). Swap them for KayKit models driven by KayKit animations. Assets are staged by the director under combat/battle/models/kaykit/ (CC0; CREDITS.md row exists). Do not add or download other assets.

## Mapping (director decisions, do not redesign)
Allies (faction ally):
- knight -> characters/Knight.glb, weapon sword_1handed + shield (round or badge) in hand slots
- mage -> characters/Mage.glb, weapon staff
- ranger -> characters/Ranger.glb, weapon bow_withString
- rogue -> characters/Rogue.glb, dagger in each hand
- cleric -> characters/Mage.glb + wand (PROVISIONAL, no free cleric model; game-designer call later)
Enemies (faction enemy): knight -> Skeleton_Warrior (+Skeleton_Blade, Skeleton_Shield_Small_A), rogue -> Skeleton_Rogue (+Skeleton_Blade), mage -> Skeleton_Mage (+Skeleton_Staff), ranger -> Skeleton_Rogue (+Skeleton_Crossbow).
Use the model's own hand bone attachments (BoneAttachment3D on handslot.r / handslot.l or whatever the rig names them; read the rig, do not guess).

Clips (all Rig_Medium, one shared AnimationLibrary loaded once, static, not re-imported per unit):
- idle: Idle_A (skeleton enemies: Skeletons_Idle)
- moving: Running_A (skeleton enemies: Skeletons_Walking)

- hit (_react / recoil): Hit_A, critical Hit_B
- dead: Death_A then hold last frame (skeleton enemies: Skeletons_Death then hold)
- downed ally: Death_B then hold; revive back to idle
Clips must play in place. If a clip moves the root, pin it; report which ones did.

## Keep
HP bars, chip, selection/elite/telegraph rings, guard bubble, downed marker, lunge, recoil, hit-stop, set_time_scale (animation speed must follow _time_scale()). Public API of BattleUnitView unchanged: set_actor, hit_stop, set_time_scale, lunge, set_selected.

title: Battle view: smooth live playback, punchier effects, smaller damage numbers
description:
Owner play-test 2026-09-23: movement looks choppy, battle feels too fast, hit-stop / lunge / wave-clear slow-mo not noticeable, damage numbers a bit big. HP bars OK.

ROOT CAUSE (director): live battles advance in 0.25s chunks (GameSession EXPEDITION_PULSE_SECONDS, systems/game_session.gd:21) and the view polls every 0.25s (BATTLE_PULSE_SECONDS, combat/battle/battle_view.gd:20). So 2-3 sim ticks land at once. Units then exponential-lerp (battle_unit_view.gd:201, rate 8/s): dash then stop, 4x a second. Every hit in the chunk fires on the same frame, so 0.06s hit-stop and lunges overlap and vanish.

FIX (view only, sim untouched, no save keys):
1. Live mode plays back one pulse behind: positions move linearly from the last snapshot to the new one over the pulse, no dash-and-stop. Practice mode (every frame) must stay correct.
2. VFX events play at their own tick time inside the pulse (offset = (event tick - first tick) * battle_tick_seconds), not all on one frame.
3. Punch tuning so each is visible: hit-stop, lunge distance, wave-clear slow-mo length/scale. Pick values, list old->new.
4. Damage numbers ~25-30% smaller (normal and crit); crit stays clearly bigger than normal.
Do NOT change battle pace/sim speed: owner re-judges pace after smoothing.

ACCEPT: BUILT (import gate + full GUT with APPDATA redirect) green; tests for the interpolation and event offset; no Engine.time_scale; real save untouched; no Godot left running.
notes: 2026-09-24 applied (view-only). Unit: linear glide from drawn position to new sim position over one render interval (live BATTLE_PULSE_SECONDS 0.25, practice battle_tick_seconds 0.1), first placement snaps (fixes fly-in from origin); per-unit reaction_delay so flash/recoil/squash/death play at the unit's hit tick. View: events_between stamps tick; delay=(tick-first_tick)*step, step=min(tick_s, glide/ticks) so hitches squeeze inside the interval; queue in _process (real time); slow-mo waits for last death; basic_attack carries target crit. title: Skills 2: the Cleric gets Mend and Grace (it has no battle ability today)
description:
Found by ig-8lj (2026-09-23). Cleric is the 5th summonable archetype (heroes/defs/cleric.tres, summon 1-in-5) but BattleSimulation.ABILITIES has no cleric entry, so it fights with basic attacks only. GAME_SPEC says Back/Heal.

DESIGNED 2026-09-23 under the skill system (ig-gy0). SYSTEMS.md § Skills, Cleric kit:
- Grace (passive): +20% to the Cleric's own heals and shields.
- Mend (ability, the Cleric's signature): 8 s cooldown, range 6, heal 3.0 x ATK to one ally. The AI uses it on the lowest-HP ally in range below heal_below (0.35), in the support pass, after revive and before items. Mend's 3.0 ATK is 48 HP at base ATK 16.
All PROVISIONAL.

BEHAVIOR
1. Two skill .tres files in the ig-gy0.1 data format. The Cleric's archetype default kit = Grace + Mend.
2. A heal primitive, if ig-gy0.1 did not add one. Healing never raises HP past max and never touches a downed ally (that is revive).
3. The heal shows through the existing view contract: last_skill_tick, and a VFX mapping in battle_vfx.gd.
4. Mend can be Manual like any signature.

ACCEPTANCE
- A test: a Cleric heals a hurt ally by 3.0 x ATK x 1.2 (Grace), capped at max HP; it does not heal above heal_below; its cooldown holds 8 s.
- The ig-544 golden cases without a Cleric are unchanged.
- A five-hero team with a Cleric: forecast still runs within 2x the ig-gy0.1 baseline.
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass (boundary #4).

NON-GOALS
The rest of the Cleric kit (ig-gy0.2); a revive (Rekindle is a book skill).

title: Arena attack clips are stretched 3-4x to fit the balance windows; trim them instead
description:
Root cause of 'combat feels clunky' after the Mixamo swap (played 2026-09-05, play pass 4).

arena.gd:_play_animation() sets custom_speed = animation.length / target_duration, so every
attack plays the WHOLE Mixamo clip (stance -> windup -> swing -> return to stance) squeezed
into the balance window that was authored for capsules. Measured native lengths (headless,
2026-09-05) against the windows they are forced into:

  Attack_A  1.500 s -> 0.42 s  (3.6x)   light chain
  Attack_B  1.667 s -> 0.42 s  (4.0x)
  Attack_C  1.367 s -> 0.42 s  (3.3x)
  Attack_Heavy 1.000 s -> 0.92 s (1.1x) -- the one that reads fine, and the user agrees
  Standing Dodge Fwd/L/R ~1.0 s -> 0.38 s (2.6x); Backward 1.633 s -> 0.38 s (4.3x)
  Block (enemy parry) 1.400 s -> 0.20 s (7x, a twitch)
  Attack_A (enemy) 1.500 s -> 1.10 s (1.4x) -- but peak extension does not land at the
    0.55 s active onset SYSTEMS.md 'the t ~= 0.55 s alignment target' rules it should
  Hit_Chest (hero) plays at NATIVE 0.767 s but hit stun is 0.35 s, so Idle cuts it in half
  Block (hero) native 1.4 s, parry lasts ~0.65 s, cut mid-raise

The 0.06 s crossfade is a hard cut at 4x. The heavy is the proof: the one clip near native
speed is the one that feels right.

Fix, smallest that works: a per-clip trim table {clip: [start_s, end_s]} in arena.gd.
In _bind_animation_libraries set animation.length = end (Godot Animation has no trim API)
and in _play_animation seek(start) after play(). Stretch the TRIMMED swing segment into the
window, not the whole clip. The Mixamo attacks have ~0.5-0.7 s of actual swing, so light
attacks land near 1.3x instead of 4x. Give hero Hit_Chest a target_duration of
arena_enemy_hit_stun. Trim enemy Block to the shield raise (~0.3 s). Set the enemy Attack_A
trim so its peak lands at t = 0.55 s, which also closes the SYSTEMS.md alignment target.

The trim values need eyes on each clip in the editor (or a played guess, then tune). That
is the authored step; the code is ~20 lines. No AnimationTree, no new clips, no balance
changes. ig-e5u (AnimationTree, 8-way) stays separate and blocked on the backpedal asset.

Acceptance: import gate + GUT green; test_arena.gd's hit-stop resume test still passes
(seek after play must not break assigned_animation resume); a played light chain reads as
three swings, not three twitches; enemy contact reads as caused by the visible blade.
Boundary: none crossed (no save, no scene rename, no autoload). verifier optional.
notes:
2026-09-05 code landed, uncommitted, awaiting a played pass.
Director re-ran both gates on the final tree: import_gate.ps1 exit 0; GUT 204/204 passing.
Files: combat/arena/arena.gd (CLIP_TRIMS table, length trim in bind, seek-on-fresh-start in _play_animation, hero Hit_Chest fitted to arena_enemy_hit_stun), tests/unit/test_arena.gd (span helper, 1 new test).
Stretch now: lights ~1.1-1.7x (was 3.3-4x), dodges ~1.6x (was 2.6-4.3x), enemy Block 1x (was 7x), enemy Attack_A contact at 0.5395 s vs the 0.55 s target.

Finding: Block is a held guard pose with no raise motion at all. A real shield raise needs a new clip; out of scope.

Known ceiling: _play_animation decides 'fresh start' by assigned_animation changing. That is only correct because the state machine always plays Idle/locomotion for at least one frame between two uses of the same clip. If a future state ever chains the same clip back to back, the second play starts from the clip's frame 0 (stance) instead of the trim start. ponytail: fix then by also treating a finished clip as fresh.

Close when a played pass says the light chain reads as swings and enemy contact reads as caused by the blade. Trim values may then move.

title: Ledger budget test is flaky: its empty baseline swings 0.8-3.5 ms, wider than the 2 ms margin
description:
WHY
test_ledger_file.gd test_a_full_ledger_adds_at_most_2_ms_to_a_commit_or_a_periodic_save failed once in the director's BUILT (2026-09-24, wgj.11 tree): on the idle save, the empty case took 0.838 ms and the mixed cap 3.240, a 2.402 gap against a 2.0 limit. It passed on a re-run.

- The eventful cap is also a full ledger, but it holds steady at 0.7 to 1.0.
So the baseline is mostly warm-up noise, and the test passes because that noise pads it. Against a clean baseline, the mixed cap's idle and periodic saves cost 1.2 to 3.2 ms. The 2 ms budget in SYSTEMS § The Ledger may really be broken for a mixed ledger.

FIX
1. godot-tester: make the test honest. Warm up before the empty timing by running one _timings() and throwing it away, so the baseline is clean.
2. Then check whether the mixed cap still breaks 2 ms. If it does, find why a save with nothing new costs about 2 ms more with a mixed full ledger than with an eventful one. The test's own comment says eventful is the eviction's worst case. Fix that, or take the budget to the game-designer.
