title: Town builder 5b: starvation, warned and never offline
description:
WHY
Slice 2 of ig-6m2.5. Read the parent first. The owner ruled that heroes can starve to death. This slice makes that fair: every death is warned, the next victim is named ahead of time, and nobody dies while the player is not looking. It crosses boundaries #1 (save) and #3 (permadeath).

BEHAVIOR
1. The clock. It is pure, in TownRules, and GameSession calls it only from _advance_clocks_in_memory. Each tick:
   - Every workplace's production (wood, stone, food) is multiplied by starving_work_multiplier while starving.
   - Demand not met (food would go below 0): food = 0, and town_starving_seconds += delta, up to the next stop point (item 2).
   - food ≥ food_low_warning_minutes × the current eating per minute: town_starving_seconds = 0 and town_starve_acked = false.
   - In between: the clock holds.
   - Starving means town_starving_seconds > 0 (SYSTEMS § Food and starvation). So work doesn't flicker between half and full speed.
2. Deaths are due at fixed points. Death n (from 1) is due at starve_first_death_minutes + (n − 1) × starve_next_death_minutes of starving: 20, 30, 40 minutes.
   - n is derived, not saved: n − 1 = how many due points the clock has already reached (a death happens as the clock reaches its point).
   - The stop point is due_n − starve_last_warning_minutes (15, 25, 35). Unless acked, the clock never passes it. Any delta is capped there, so a long tick or a hitch can't skip a warning.
3. acknowledge_starvation(). It does something only while the clock sits at a stop point, and is a no-op otherwise. It sets town_starve_acked through _commit_profile_mutation. Once acked, the clock runs to due_n.
4. The death. When the clock reaches due_n:
   - victim = TownRules.starvation_victim(eaters), using slice 1's eater read. It is pure and returns an instance_id or "". Order: lowest rank, then lowest level, then newest in the roster (the last in roster order).
   - GameSession unequips every equipped item to inventory through unequip_item, then calls kill_hero(hero, &"", balance, "starvation"). Nothing is equipped by then, so no Lost Cache.
   - town_starve_acked = false. The status line says "<name> starved."
   - No other code removes a hero (rule 8). If the victim is the body, kill_hero already clears the body.
5. The ladder. It is built in code in hub_ui_builder.gd, like the recovery-clock warning, so hub.tscn does not change. It refreshes on the tick signals.
   - "Food low": food < food_low_warning_minutes × eating per minute, while anyone eats.
   - "Starving": work at half speed, plus who dies next and when ("Mira starves in 12:30 unless the town is fed").
   - "Last warning": stopped at a stop point. It says who and when, and has a button that calls acknowledge_starvation().
6. Numbers. Add food_low_warning_minutes 10, starving_work_multiplier 0.5, starve_first_death_minutes 20, starve_next_death_minutes 10 and starve_last_warning_minutes 5 to balance_table.gd and balance.tres. Keep other people's uncommitted work intact.

SAVE (boundary #1)
- town_starving_seconds and town_starve_acked are additive keys: no SAVE_VERSION bump.
- town_starving_seconds: missing → 0. Not finite, or < 0 → 0, with a warning. Past the next stop point while not acked → the stop point, so a save can't skip a warning.
- town_starve_acked: missing, or not a bool → false. True while the clock is not at a stop point → false. It only ever means "this warning was seen".
- ig-6pm: these are repairs, never refusals (no validate_saved_state rule). Every value written is one the load keeps as it is.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- The clock:
  - food 0 with demand unmet: the clock advances by delta;
  - a farm that makes less than the town eats still starves (food ticks above 0 but never reaches the food-low line);
  - food above the line resets the clock;
  - in between, the clock holds.
- Starving halves wood, stone and food production. After the reset, full speed.
- Ladder:
  - the clock stops at 15:00, and stays there over any number of ticks and one huge delta;
  - an ack starts it again, and the death comes at 20:00;
  - the next stop is at 25:00, and after another ack the death comes at 30:00.
- AFK: an offline catch-up of any length moves neither food nor the clock. Hours of live ticks with no ack kill nobody past the first stop.
- Victim:
  - order is rank, then level, then newest;
  - away, busy and unhoused heroes are never picked.
- The death:
  - the victim's gear is in inventory, and there is no Lost Cache;
  - the Ledger holds a 'died' record with cause "starvation";
  - a victim who is the body leaves no body behind.
- grep: roster.erase appears only in kill_hero.
- Save:
  - a real disk save and reload stopped at a last warning keeps food, the clock and acked false, and the clock is still stopped;
  - a save and reload after the ack keeps acked true;
  - repairs: clock -1 → 0; a clock past the stop with acked false → the stop; acked true below the stop → false; no keys → 0 and false.
- A screenshot of each ladder state, in .agent-results/ig-6m2.5.2/.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundaries #1 and #3.

FILES
- hub/town/town_rules.gd (the clock step, the victim)
- systems/game_session.gd, balance_table.gd, balance.tres
- hub/hub_ui_builder.gd (the ladder line and its button; keep the uncommitted work already in it)
- hub/hub.gd (refresh, the ack, the status line)
- tests/unit/test_town_food.gd; tests/save_roundtrip_check.gd if the disk case lives there

Everything in the parent's NON-GOALS.

title: Town builder 5a: farms and food
description:
WHY
Slice 1 of ig-6m2.5. Read the parent first. The town gets food: Farms make it, and housed heroes who are home eat it. In this slice, food that runs out just stays at 0. Slice 2 adds starvation, so the permadeath change gets its own small review.

BEHAVIOR
1. The Farm. FARM (&"Farm") joins TownRules.TYPES and FREE_FIRST, with wood_cost = farm_wood_cost and worker_slots = farm_worker_slots. Ids are Farm_N. Workers follow the Lumbermill and Mine rules: a House first, protected not busy, paused while away. The build menu reads TYPES.
2. Scene. New hub/town/buildings/farm.tscn, built like mine.tscn:
   - Model = building_grain.gltf at ×3.0, plus Label;
   - Pick: a StaticBody3D on layer 2 with a 4.5 × 3 × 4.5 box;
   - WorkSpot: a Marker3D at (0, 0, 2.8).
   Add it to TownView.SCENES.
3. Food. town_resources gains "food". One pure step in TownRules:
   food_step(food, farm workers home, eaters, delta, balance) = max(food + made − eaten, 0), where
   - made = food_per_worker_minute × farm workers home × minutes;
   - eaten = food_per_housed_hero_minute × eaters × minutes.
   GameSession calls it only from _advance_clocks_in_memory, never from the offline catch-up.
4. Eaters. A GameSession read (e.g. food_eaters()) returns the housed heroes (home != NO_HOME) who are not is_hero_busy. Slice 2 reuses it.
5. HUD. The resource label adds food ("Wood: 12   Stone: 3   Food: 23"). A Farm's placed panel says "Makes 1.0 food a minute", from the type-driven line .3.1 built.
6. Walker clip. If ig-6m2.6.1 has landed, add Farm → Digging to town_walker.gd's clip table, and Digging (Rig_Medium_Tools) to HeroModel.CLIP_FILES and LOOPED_CLIPS.
7. Numbers. Add town_start_food 30, food_per_housed_hero_minute 0.2, farm_wood_cost 20, farm_worker_slots 2 and food_per_worker_minute 1.0 to balance_table.gd and balance.tres (SYSTEMS § Food and starvation). Keep other people's uncommitted work in those files intact.

SAVE (boundary #1)
- town_resources.food is an additive key: no SAVE_VERSION bump.
- If the food key is missing, whether or not town_resources exists, the save gets town_start_food, once. That is not how wood and stone work: a missing key inside an existing town_resources gives them 0. It has to differ, because every ig-6m2.3.1-era save has town_resources with no food, and those saves must start with 30.
- If present, read it with Item.float_field and clamp it at 0.
- ig-6pm: repair, never refuse. Add no validate_saved_state rule.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)

- Eating:

  - a dispatched hero, a hero in a battle and an unhoused hero eat nothing;
  - unhousing a hero stops its eating.
- A Farm with one housed worker at home makes 1.0 a minute. Food never goes below 0.
- An offline catch-up of any length moves food 0.
- Save:
  - a real disk save and reload keeps food;
  - a save with town_resources but no food loads 30;
  - a save with no town_resources loads wood 40 and food 30;
  - food -3 loads 0.
- farm.tscn: the Pick is on layer 2 only, a WorkSpot exists, and building_at names Farm_1.

title: Town builder 3b: buildings take live-play time to go up
description:
WHY
Slice 2 of ig-6m2.3. Read the parent first. A new House or workplace takes live-play time to go up, and you can see it happen: scaffolding, then three stages, then its own model. Until it is finished it does nothing.

BEHAVIOR
1. Placing. place_building sets build_remaining on the new building's dict, from TownRules.build_seconds(type, balance):
   - house_build_seconds for a House;
   - workplace_build_seconds for every workplace type (TownRules.worker_slots(type) > 0). That covers the Lumbermill and the Mine, and the Farm too, whichever of this slice and ig-6m2.5.1 lands first.
   Halls are never placed, so they are never under construction.
2. The clock.
   - _advance_clocks_in_memory takes delta off every build_remaining. At 0 the key is erased, and the building is finished.
   - The offline catch-up (_advance_orders_in_memory) does not touch it.
   - The live tick already emits roster_changed, so the town and the panels refresh without a new signal.
3. Under construction = the key is present.
   - station_hero and assign_home refuse with a reason, e.g. "House 3 is still being built (0:42 left)."
   - Its hex is taken. Placing there is refused, as today.
   - move_building works and keeps build_remaining (it only changes q and r).
   - It counts as having one for the free rule. TownRules already counts any building of the type.
   - A Lumbermill or Mine under construction can have no workers, so it makes nothing.
4. The look.
   - TownView.show_buildings shows a building under construction as its type's scene, with the Model hidden and a Stage model in its place.
   - The stage follows how much is done: building_scaffolding for the first quarter of the build time, then building_stage_A, _B and _C. When it finishes, the Model shows again. Stage = floor(done fraction × 4), clamped to 0..3.
   - Hexagon models are ×3.0, as ig-wgj.3 set.
   - Label, Pick and WorkSpot don't change.
   - show_buildings runs on every tick (roster_changed), so it swaps the stage node only when the stage changes. Otherwise it does nothing.
5. Panel. A building under construction shows "Under construction: 0:42 left" in its placed panel, and Assign is disabled.
6. Numbers. Add house_build_seconds 60 and workplace_build_seconds 120 to balance_table.gd and balance.tres. Keep other people's uncommitted work intact.

SAVE (boundary #1)
- build_remaining is an additive key on a building dict, in seconds. No SAVE_VERSION bump.
- to_dict writes it only while it is > 0. A missing key means finished, so every older building loads finished.
- Today _read_town_building builds a new dict holding only id, type, q and r. It must carry build_remaining too:
  - a finite number > 0 is kept, clamped to that type's build seconds (a lower tuned time never leaves a longer wait);
  - a missing key, 0 or less, or a non-number means finished: drop the key, and warn on a bad value;
  - on a hall, it is ignored.
- ig-6pm: keep this a repair, not a refusal (no validate_saved_state rule), so a written save always loads. build_remaining is maxf(finite − delta, 0), so it stays finite.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- A placed House has build_remaining 60, and every workplace type in TownRules.TYPES has 120. A hall has none.
- The live tick moves it 1 s per s, and it finishes (key gone) at 0. An offline catch-up of any length moves it 0.
- Under construction, assign_home and station_hero refuse with the reason and change no state. After it finishes, both work.
- Moving a building under construction leaves build_remaining unchanged.
- Free rule: while the free Lumbermill is under construction, a second one costs full price. The preview equals the result.
- Save:
  - a half-built House (build_remaining 30) survives a real disk save and reload with 30;
  - an ig-6m2.3.1-era save loads every building finished;
  - bad values on a House (−1, "x", 1e9) load as finished, finished and 60.
- The look:
  - at 0 %, 25 %, 50 % and 75 % done, the stage node is scaffolding, stage_A, stage_B and stage_C;
  - at 100 % the Model shows and the stage node is gone;
  - a tick that doesn't cross a quarter keeps the same stage node.
- Screenshots of the four stages and the finished House, in .agent-results/ig-6m2.3.2/.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #1 (build_remaining, the legacy save) and #2 (the stage node in the building scenes).

FILES
- systems/game_session.gd, hub/town/town_rules.gd, balance_table.gd, balance.tres
- hub/town/town_view.gd (the stage node)
- hub/hub.gd (the placed panel)
- new hub/town/models/hexagon/building_scaffolding.gltf + .bin and building_stage_A.gltf + .bin (parent § Assets)
- tests/unit: test_town_builder.gd, or a new test_town_construction.gd

NON-GOALS
Builders or hauling (it just takes time). Cancelling, refunding or rushing. Construction for halls or upgrades. Build time for moving. Everything in the parent's NON-GOALS.

title: The body cannot walk to buildings near the map edge (fixed 23.6 m walk bounds)
description:
Found by extra while scoping ig-6m2.6 (2026-09-24). hub/town/town_view.gd:37 WALK_HALF_EXTENT = 23.6 sets the player body's bounds (town_view.gd:120-121) as a fixed square. The hex map (town_map_radius 8) reaches about 30 m, at hex (5,0) for example. Since ig-6m2.2 any building can move to any free hex, so a building placed near the edge is out of the body's reach, and so is a partner standing out there.

Fix: derive the bounds from the map geometry (TownRules map hexes and the hex size) instead of a constant, so every placeable hex is reachable. Keep it the simplest rule that works (a bounding rect of the map plus one hex is fine; corners past the hex map are harmless ground).

Acceptance: a test that the body can reach the centre of the farthest map hex in each direction; test_town_hero's edge test updated to the derived bound; BUILT green. Scene seam (#2) is not touched unless the fix moves nodes.

title: Town walkers 2: wanderers, the partner as a walker, click a walker
description:
WHY
Slice 2 of ig-6m2.6. Read the parent first. The rest of the town comes alive: heroes in town with no job wander and use the halls. The bond partner becomes an ordinary walker, so nothing stands at a fixed spot a building can swallow (the ig-6m2.2 note on the parent). A click on a walker opens that hero. This is what ig-wgj.5 asked for, rebuilt on slice 1's hex walk graph.

BEHAVIOR
1. Wanderers. Every in-town hero with no station gets a figure, up to the cap.
   - It walks to a free hex that touches a building (the streets, not the empty map edge), picked by its own RNG. It lingers LINGER_SECONDS, then picks again.
   - If that hex is an approach hex of a hall, it faces the hall and plays Interact (it is using the stall). Elsewhere it plays Idle_B.
   - A wanderer with a House ends one trip in HOME_EVERY at its door (Idle_A).
   - First show: each wanderer starts at a street hex from its own RNG. Later joiners come in at the TownGate, as in slice 1.
   - A wanderer who gets stationed re-plans from where it stands. It does not re-enter at the gate.
2. Cap. AMBIENT_HERO_CAP, a constant in town_view.gd, counts wanderers only. Keepers, workers and the partner always show.
   - hub.gd passes the in-town heroes in pick order: keepers and workers, the partner, then favorites, then higher rank, then lower instance_id. The same heroes appear each visit.
   - FPS: measure at caps 8, 12 and 16 in a windowed run, with APPDATA pointed at a throwaway folder holding a seeded save with enough heroes. Never the owner's real APPDATA.
   - Set the cap to the highest value that holds 60 FPS. Mark it PROVISIONAL in the code comment, and put the numbers in these notes.
3. The partner is its own walker. hub.gd stops leaving the partner out. show_partner hands the line and the body to the partner's walker.
   - The greeting keeps what ig-m6o.2.1 built: MEET_DISTANCE, REARM_DISTANCE, LINE_SECONDS, Interact once, the line above its head. The greeting pauses the walk, and the walk resumes after it.
   - A partner that starts inside REARM_DISTANCE of the body starts disarmed, so a load never fires the greeting at once.
   - Drop PARTNER_SPAWN_OFFSET, PARTNER_DOOR_OFFSET and the fixed placement in show_partner. The partner works, rests or wanders by its role, like everyone else. One figure per hero.
   - Fold town_partner.gd into town_walker.gd, or keep it as a greeter the walker owns: implementer's choice.
4. Click a walker. Each figure gets a pick shape on a new WALKER_PICK_LAYER. The body stays on no layer.
   - One ray over both pick layers; the nearest hit wins.
   - A walker hit emits a new hero_selected(hero_id), and hub.gd opens that hero's detail. A building hit still emits building_selected.
   - With a body embodied, a walker click opens the detail at once, with no walk.
   - This changes ig-wgj.7 item 4 ("clicking a keeper emits building_selected for its building"). A keeper stands in front of its building, which is still one click away. Director: confirm, or keepers and workers open their building and only wanderers open the hero.
5. Numbers: LINGER_SECONDS, HOME_EVERY and AMBIENT_HERO_CAP stay in the view scripts (parent § Rules).

ACCEPTANCE (extend tests/unit/test_town_walkers.gd; change tests/unit/test_bonds.gd)
- Wanderers use only free ground: 60 s of simulated wandering, sampled every 0.25 m, never inside a grown box. At a hall's approach hex a wanderer faces the hall and plays Interact.
- Cap and order: with more unemployed heroes in town than the cap, the shown set matches the pick order. Keepers, workers and the partner show beyond the cap. The set updates after a dispatch, a return, a summon and a kill_hero.
- Partner:
  - exactly one figure for the partner hero;
  - it greets once when the walking body comes within MEET_DISTANCE, pauses and resumes, and re-arms past REARM_DISTANCE;
  - it starts disarmed inside REARM_DISTANCE;
  - the ig-6m2.2 case: move the Sanctum off (1, 0) and a House onto it, and the partner is never inside a box;
  - replace the fixed-spot asserts at test_bonds.gd:218 and :287.
- Click: a click on a walker emits hero_selected with its id and opens its detail. A click on a building still names the building. A walker in front of its building wins the click. Pick click points as the bd memory headless-gut-click-tests says (GUT's output panel eats clicks).
- Nothing saved and the global RNG untouched, as in slice 1, now with wanderers.
- The FPS numbers and the chosen cap in these notes. A screenshot of the town with wanderers in .agent-results/ig-6m2.6.2/.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #2 (the new signal, the pick layer, the hub wiring).

FILES
- hub/town/town_view.gd: the cap, the walker pick, hero_selected, the partner through its walker, the partner offsets dropped
- hub/town/town_walker.gd: wandering, the greeting
- hub/town/town_partner.gd (+ .gd.uid): folded in, or kept as the walker's greeter
- hub/hub.gd: pick order, the partner no longer left out, hero_selected → detail
- tests/unit/test_town_walkers.gd, tests/unit/test_bonds.gd

NON-GOALS
Heroes talking to or reacting to each other. Wanderers reacting to the body (only the partner greets). Everything in the parent's NON-GOALS.

title: Town walkers 1: keepers and workers walk House to work and back
description:
WHY
Slice 1 of ig-6m2.6. Read the parent first: it holds the shared rules and the walkable-area ruling. The town looks like it works. Every keeper and worker in town is drawn at its building, walking to it from its House and back. This is ig-wgj.7's scope, rebuilt on the builder's per-scene WorkSpot.

BEHAVIOR
1. Walk graph. TownView builds the AStar2D and updates it in show_buildings (parent § The walkable area). It exposes two reads over the current occupancy, both testable without frames:
   - route(from, to), where each end is a building's WorkSpot (reached through its approach hexes) or a free-ground point;
   - free_point(near).
   The six axial directions may live in TownRules as a constant (hex math only).
2. Figures. New TownWalker (hub/town/town_walker.gd): a Node3D holding the HeroModel, with the archetype picked as TownHero.create does and the same MODEL_SCALE. No physics body. It follows its route at WALK_SPEED playing Walking_A, faces where it walks, and plays its activity clip on arrival.
3. show_walkers(heroes: Array[Hero]). hub.gd passes every in-town hero with a station (keepers and workers), except the bond partner, which keeps its TownPartner figure until slice 2.
   - A refresh keeps an existing figure and its walk. It re-plans only a hero whose station or House changed.
   - It frees the figures of heroes no longer in the list.
   - expeditions_changed fires on every 0.25 s pulse, so a refresh that changes nothing must do nothing.
4. The loop, per figure:
   - A House and a route both ways: walk from the House door to the work spot, work WORK_SECONDS, walk back, rest at the door HOME_SECONDS (Idle_A, facing out), repeat.
   - No House (hall keepers may have none), or no route: stand at the work spot and work. No route = no free approach hex, or the free ground is cut in two. No error, no warning.
   - The work clip comes from a station → clip table in town_walker.gd. A station missing from the table plays Working_A, so a later workplace (the Mine, the Farm) never breaks a figure; those slices add their own row. Suggested: Forge Hammering, Lumbermill Chopping, Apothecary Working_A, Training Hall Push_Ups, Sanctum Sit_Floor_Idle, Reliquary Working_C. Change any on sight.
5. Where a figure starts:
   - First show after the town opens: at work, a random way into WORK_SECONDS from its own RNG. A reload doesn't stream everyone in, and they don't all walk home together.
   - A hero who joins later (back from an expedition, or newly stationed): at the TownGate's WorkSpot, walking to its place.
   - A hero who just stopped being the body: where the body stood. embody() keeps the removed body's hero id and position for the next show_walkers.
6. A place or a move re-plans every figure from where it stands: first to the centre of the hex it is on, then on. A worker whose building moved walks to the new spot. Anyone on a hex that just got a building, other than at that building's own WorkSpot, moves to free_point(where it stood). That includes the body: placing does not step out of the body (hub._on_build_picked keeps it), so a building can land on it today.
7. Wiring. New hub._refresh_walkers: connect it to roster_changed right after _refresh_town, and to expeditions_changed ahead of _show_partner. In _ready, call it after _refresh_town() and before _refresh_partner(). Then embody has run (the step-out record) and show_buildings has run (the graph), and slice 2's partner will find its walker.
8. Clips. Add the table's clips to HeroModel.CLIP_FILES and LOOPED_CLIPS: Hammering, Chopping, Working_A and Working_C from Rig_Medium_Tools; Push_Ups and Sit_Floor_Idle from Rig_Medium_Simulation. Check each loops cleanly. If one doesn't, swap in another from the same file (Tools also has Sawing, Digging, Working_B; Simulation has Sit_Chair_Idle).
9. Numbers: WALK_SPEED, WORK_SECONDS, HOME_SECONDS and the clip table are constants in town_walker.gd (parent § Rules).

ACCEPTANCE (new tests/unit/test_town_walkers.gd; APPDATA redirected as always)
- Around, not through: default halls, plus a House and a Lumbermill with a hall between them. Sample the House → Lumbermill route every 0.25 m. No sample is inside any building's box grown by 0.3 m, and the route ends at the WorkSpot.
- Placed and moved: place a building on a hex the route crosses, and the new route passes the same check. Move the Lumbermill, and its worker's destination is the new WorkSpot.
- Built over: a figure standing on a free hex that gets a building ends on free ground (outside every grown box). So does the body.
- Walled in: fill both approach hexes of a building. Its worker stands at the spot working, and nothing is logged.
- The set follows the state:
  - station → a figure at work (first show);
  - unstation, dispatch, kill_hero → no figure;
  - a return → a figure at the TownGate's WorkSpot;
  - the body and the partner never get a figure.
- Step out: the old body's figure appears where the body stood.
- Quiet pulse: a show_walkers with an unchanged list keeps every figure's node and destination.
- Nothing saved: drive the walkers' step directly for 10 s of simulated time, with no GameSession tick. GameSession.to_dict() is identical before and after. town_walker.gd has no GameSession reference.
- Global RNG untouched: seed(1234), drive the walkers 300 steps, then randi() equals the randi() right after a fresh seed(1234).
- Clips: every clip in the table is in HeroModel.shared_clips() and loops.
- test_town_hero.gd and test_bonds.gd stay green, unchanged.
- Screenshots in .agent-results/ig-6m2.6.1/: workers at work, and one mid-walk.
- BUILT. Verifier pass mandatory: boundary #2 (the hub.gd wiring and order, the WorkSpot reads, the HeroModel library).

FILES
- hub/town/town_view.gd: graph, route, free_point, show_walkers, the built-over rule, the step-out record
- new hub/town/town_walker.gd (+ .gd.uid)
- heroes/hero_model.gd: the clip table only
- hub/hub.gd: _refresh_walkers and its wiring
- optional: hub/town/town_rules.gd, the six axial directions
- new tests/unit/test_town_walkers.gd
- No .tscn change: every building scene already has its WorkSpot.

NON-GOALS
Heroes with no job (slice 2). The partner, including its fixed spot (slice 2 fixes that). Clicking a figure (slice 2). A cap: keepers and workers are bounded by buildings (five halls, two per Lumbermill). Everything in the parent's NON-GOALS.

title: A save can write a state its own loader refuses (the save path skips validate_saved_state)
description:
Found by high1 during ig-wgj.10 (2026-09-24). A test fixture with a bad stranded incident committed through _commit_profile_mutation and saved fine, then load_game refused the same file ('squad_id must match squad membership'). So the write side never runs the loader's validation. In play this only matters if a bug ever makes in-memory state invalid, but then the next save writes a file the game will not load, and the player is locked out of the save (boundary #1).

Question for godot-architect first: should SaveService (or _commit_profile_mutation) run validate_saved_state on the dict before writing, and on failure refuse the save so the existing rollback undoes the action? That turns 'a bug locks the save' into 'a bug refuses one action'. Weigh the cost of a full validation on every save.

Related, lower: Sol (ig-wgj.10 round 1) noted validate_saved_state does not check hero profession_xp. Hero.from_dict loads a bad value as 0 with push_error by design, so a bad XP number is zeroed rather than refused. Rule whether that stays.

Acceptance, if the answer is yes: a test that corrupts in-memory state, runs a real action, and shows the save refused, the action rolled back and the file on disk still loadable (APPDATA redirected). BUILT green. Verifier pass on boundary #1.
notes:
ARCHITECT RULING (2026-09-24): yes, check before writing. Put it in SaveService.save(), not in _commit_profile_mutation. No boundary moves, so no ADR.

WHERE, AND WHY THERE
- save() is the one door every writer uses: _commit_profile_mutation (every action, plus tick_expeditions when something falls due), the 15 s periodic save and its retry (game_session.gd ~95-120), the roster_changed signal save (_ready), and load_game's legacy-migration save. A check in _commit_profile_mutation would miss the last three.
- The rules stay in GameSession.validate_saved_state. SaveService already calls it on load (save_service.gd:130-131), so on save it only calls the same thing. The invariant "SaveService never writes a file its own load refuses" is file integrity, which is SaveService's job (ARCHITECTURE rule 4). It is not a game rule, and the autoload rule holds.
- Quit: nothing extra. The game does not save on quit (main_menu.gd:26 just quits, and nothing handles WM_CLOSE), so the per-action and periodic saves are the only writers. A quit save added later gets the guard for free.

THE EXACT RULE (save_service.gd save())
1. Build payload as today, with version and saved_at_unix set. Then text = JSON.stringify(payload, "\t").
2. Before the ledger write, check what load will read: parsed = JSON.parse_string(text). Not a Dictionary → refuse. Otherwise GameSession.repair_rescue_timestamps(parsed), then GameSession.validate_saved_state(parsed, SAVE_VERSION); a non-empty result → refuse. Put parse → repair → validate in one small helper that load_game (130-134) uses too, so the two can never drift.
3. Refuse = _write_failed("Save refused: this game state would not load (<reason>). Your last save is safe; restart to return to it.") and return false. It runs before the ledger write, so a refusal touches no file and needs no _undo_ledger.
4. Write the same text to TMP_PATH (no second stringify).
5. Check the round trip, not the in-memory dict. The loader reads JSON text: numbers come back as floats, StringName comes back as String, and keys come back as strings. A NaN or inf may not survive stringify at all. The in-memory dict is a different object from what load sees, so checking it could refuse good states or pass bad ones.
6. Comment the check with ig-6pm and "do not remove for speed", so a later pass does not strip it.

WHAT THE PLAYER SEES
- An action: it does nothing, and last_action_error shows the message (the existing rollback, game_session.gd ~2149-2171).
- Periodic: _checkpoint_save_failed stops the world clocks, as a disk-full failure does today, and the battle views show checkpoint_error. It retries every 15 s and keeps failing until restart.
- Next main-menu visit: _load_notice shows it too (already set by _write_failed).
- Restarting loads the last good save; progress since then is lost. That is the right cost for a bug, and far better than a locked save.
- The rollback restores the pre-action snapshot. If memory went bad in an earlier signal or periodic save rather than inside this action, every later save is refused too. That is expected: the file stays good.
- No auto-repair. Silently "fixing" state hides the bug and could drop heroes (permadeath, boundary #3).

COST (acceptable; measure, don't gate)
- save() already stringifies the whole payload and writes, flushes and renames two files. The check adds one parse plus one linear walk over the same data: the same order as the stringify, and below the disk work.
- Saves happen per player action, when an order or cache falls due, and every 15 s at most. Never per frame. The 0.25 s pulse already runs BattleState.from_dict twice per order, which costs more.
- Acceptance prints save() time with and without the check on a large profile, best of seven (test_ledger.gd style). Report it in this bead. If the check costs more than the write itself, raise it with the director; don't drop the check.

REJECTED
- Check only in _commit_profile_mutation: it misses the periodic, signal and migration saves.
- Check the in-memory dict: that is not what load reads (see rule 5).
- Debug-only assert: the lock-out happens in the player's build.
- Keep a save.bak and write anyway: it still writes a file the game refuses, and needs a restore UI. Revisit only if a refusal ever shows up in play.

profession_xp: STAYS as is (zeroed with push_error, not refused)
- validate_saved_state refuses what breaks integrity: ids, cross-references, duplication, permadeath and battle checkpoints.
- Soft per-hero numbers (xp at hero.gd:527, passions, profession_xp) are repaired on load with an error log. Refusing the whole save over one bad XP number would lock the player out to protect a few minutes of one hero's hall progress. That is the failure this bead exists to remove.
- It stays consistent with the new rule, because the write check refuses only what load refuses. A soft-repaired field never blocks a save.

TESTS (APPDATA redirected; restore SAVE_PATH and LEDGER_PATH like test_battle_persistence.gd:113-121)
1. Action refused: put the ig-wgj.10 bad stranded incident in memory (squad_id vs membership), then run a real action through _commit_profile_mutation (e.g. a favorite toggle). Check: it returns false, last_action_error names the reason, the action is rolled back, save.json is byte-identical, and load_game on it succeeds.
2. Ledger untouched: in the same case, ledger.jsonl keeps its length and there is no orphan line.
3. Periodic: bad state plus an active order, then drive past PERIODIC_SAVE_SECONDS. _checkpoint_save_failed is set, checkpoint_error carries the reason, and the file is unchanged.
4. Signal save: bad state, then emit roster_changed. The file is unchanged.
5. Non-finite: set a saved float (e.g. recovery_clock_seconds) to NAN in memory and save. It is refused, and the file is unchanged.
6. Legacy migration still loads and re-saves (the existing v2 tests stay green).
7. Cost print (above).
8. BUILT + full GUT, with the determinism golden unchanged.

title: Summon and rank-up ignore a failed save (a locked save gives a free summon re-roll)
description:
From Sol's review of ig-m6o.9 (point 2; .agent-results/logs/ig-m6o.9-sol.json). Rescoped 2026-09-24 after extra traced every death path.

THE BUG
Two hub actions change the profile outside _commit_profile_mutation. They save only through the roster_changed signal, which is connected to SaveService.save (systems/game_session.gd:84) and ignores its return:
- GameSession.summon_hero, from hub/hub.gd (about line 1053)
- GameSession.rank_up_hero, from hub/hub.gd (about line 1111)
When that save fails (full disk, lock, permissions), memory runs ahead of disk with no rollback and no error. Summon is the bad one. hub.gd rolls the hero with the global randi() (Summon.roll) before any commit and shows 'Summoned X'. Quitting then undoes the pull and refunds the stones: a free re-roll by locking the save file.

NOT A BUG (the first version of this bead was wrong)
Every death already runs inside _commit_profile_mutation, so a failed save rolls it back and memory and disk agree. The director checked each path:
- abandon: :1189
- live expiry and failed rescue: the live tick, :1507
- offline catch-up: :1520
- legacy QuickResolve: _complete_order_in_memory, under both ticks
- sacrifice: _apply_bulk_plan_in_memory
The original claim came from grepping the direct kill_hero call sites without tracing the wrappers.

FIX
Route summon_hero and rank_up_hero through _commit_profile_mutation, so a failed save rolls back and reports the reason, like every other profile action.

ACCEPTANCE
- For summon and rank-up, a forced save failure leaves memory and disk agreeing and shows the reason. Prove it with a real disk reload (boundary #1).
- A summon's result is revealed only after its commit lands. No reveal or animation may come before it (the re-roll hole).
- One forced-failure GUT test per death path (abandon, live expiry, failed rescue, offline catch-up) asserts the hero is alive on disk after a reload. This locks in the guarantee above (boundary #3).
- BUILT + GUT green. Sol reviews (boundaries #1 and #3).

NOTES
- extra's design draft (2026-09-24, in the director's session) recommends an immediate pause plus a persistent 'can't save' banner on the first failed commit. Today the live tick retries silently for up to 15 s, until the periodic save fails and shows the error. That's not needed for this bug; build it only if the owner ever hits it.
- At close, game-designer records in KNOWN_ISSUES: quitting while saves fail resumes from the last save, up to 15 s back (PERIODIC_SAVE_SECONDS), the same as a crash.
notes: 2026-09-24 high: summon_hero and rank_up_hero now go through _commit_profile_mutation (_summon_in_memory/_rank_up_in_memory). rank_up_hero also refuses a Hero not on the roster (Sol finding 2: a stale object after a rollback). hub.gd reveals the pull only on true; a failed pull shows only last_action_error. Tests in test_ledger.gd: summon and rank-up through the hub buttons with a forced save failure and a real reload (both the append and the whole-rewrite ledger paths), plus abandon, live expiry, failed rescue and offline catch-up, each with a control step. BUILT: gate exit 0; GUT 599/599 (.agent-results/ig-8hj/gut_full2.log). Sol: FAIL (2 findings) -> fixed/argued -> PASS WITH NITS (.agent-results/logs/ig-8hj-sol*.json). Open: a failed rewrite leaves an orphan summoned line in ledger.jsonl until the next save; load drops it, so there is no re-roll (Sol agrees). Pre-existing nit: summon_hero accepts a Hero already on the roster. Uncommitted.
close_reason: Summon and rank-up run through _commit_profile_mutation; a failed save rolls back and shows the reason, and the hub reveals a pull only after its commit lands. Tests reload from disk: summon and rank-up (also on the whole-rewrite ledger path) and the four death paths. Director BUILT: gate exit 0, GUT 599/599 (15782 asserts), reap 0. Sol FAIL then PASS WITH NITS. Director rulings: the void pull's line left in ledger.jsonl after a failed whole rewrite needs no change (the load drops it and nothing can keep it); no duplicate-summon guard (no caller passes a roster hero). KNOWN_ISSUES entry added. Commits c19d118, 9f859eb.

title: Living-world 2: People at home (quirks, dreams, shared meals, encounters, Bonds)
description:
WHY
New feeling: affection and everyday amusement. Heroes are people at home before they are units.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction, pillar "A Home Worth Returning To" and step 2.

OPENS WITH A THIN SLICE, THEN AN OWNER GATE (director, 2026-09-24)
- Slice 1 is a thin vertical slice: ONE dream, ONE bond, ONE visible moment. For example, two housemates who shared meals and a battle become friends, and the player sees it happen in town. It is built on the Ledger.
- Then the owner plays it. The full scope below starts only if the owner says "someone worth knowing" lands. If it does not, game-designer re-plans .2 before anything else is built.
- Why: the whole direction rests on this feeling. It is cheap to test now and expensive to discover late.

SCOPE, after the gate (tech-lead splits it)
- Passions exist (ig-wgj.13). Add quirks and one dream per hero (a want with milestones).
- Meals become social events: housemates who eat together, soup factions. The Ledger's `meal` kind is written here.
- Neighbourhood encounters: heroes who live or work near each other meet, and the meeting is recorded.
- Bonds: friend, rival, collaborator, grown from recorded encounters, meals and shared battles. Bonds are derived from the Ledger plus a small saved bond state if derivation proves too slow. That choice needs an ADR.
- Joy: nicknames, petty hobbies, festivals that come out of residents' histories.
- Signature moments this step delivers: neighbours become friends and rivals; adjoining workshops invent techniques (only as a bond label in this step; real techniques come in step 3).

READS / WRITES THE LEDGER
Writes meal and encounter records, and bond-change records if bonds are events. Reads shared battles.

DEPENDS
Step 1 (the Ledger). ig-6m2.5.1 (food and eating, for meals; starvation, .5.2, is not needed). ig-6m2.6, both slices (.6.1 keepers and workers, .6.2 wanderers and the partner walker, to show encounters). These live on ig-m6o.2.2 as bd deps; the slice ig-m6o.2.1 needs none of them.

OPEN (game-designer)
- The dream catalogue and its milestone shapes.
- The number of quirks.
- Bond thresholds (PROVISIONAL).
- Whether bonds are derived or stored (ADR).

NOT HERE
Bonds changing combat (step 3). Founding a dream's institution (step 5).
notes:
2026-09-24 DIRECTION v2 (final; GAME_SPEC § Direction). Adds to the body above; where it says SUPERSEDES, v2 wins.
The thin slice and the owner gate still come first.

V2 STEP 2 LIST: spatial routines, directed relationships, knowledge, gossip, recall, moods, dreams and place imprints.
- Relationships are directed and layered: familiarity, affection, situational trust, respect, grievances, commitments, shared techniques. Roles overlap (friend, rival, partner, mentor, debtor, enemy). This widens the body's "Bonds: friend, rival, collaborator".
- A dream names its owner, formative events, desired change, beneficiaries, acceptable methods, observable milestones and the owner's reason. New knowledge can revise it (GAME_SPEC § 5).
- Moods drive routines, private goals produce actions, repeated choices become habits, all only while the game is open. Diaries describe only what their writers know and infer.
- Pulled in from step 1: witnessed details land here, with their first reader (GAME_SPEC § 10 PROVISIONAL).
- Scope boundaries: moods and dialogue (stated reasons, requests, diaries) leave GAME_SPEC § Scope boundaries only when this step's ticket is written.

A2 ITEMS ON THIS STEP (GAME_SPEC § Kept in full):
1. How gossip works [r1]. Gossip needs contact: meals, work, travel, bedside visits. Each exchange carries a bounded number of topics, picked by relevance, emotional intensity and the listener's interests. Couriers reach other districts faster; a popular tavern reaches more listeners. The screen shows who knows which claim, and through whom. Tellers bend a story to their motives (an eyewitness omits their shame, a boaster exaggerates, a partisan swaps the culprit). Detail fades with each retelling while confidence can rise. Ten people repeating one source are still one source. Memory keeps the gist and the feeling longer than the wording; varied retellings and reenactments strengthen recall more than repetition. Forgetting a betrayal does not restore trust. Belief is played through encounters: a hero shows a disputed claim and a concrete objection the player can test ("That cannot be her technique"). Bring the witness, the item or the person.
2. Profession dreams [r4]. Woodcutting, "Give us a road home": a raised connection between home and work; proof is the named residents making the once-dangerous journey. Smithing, "This shield brings you back": forge a response to an observed failure; proof is the paired sequence working and both coming home. Rites, "Let them remember whom they buried": gather witnesses, a place's imprint and departed testimony; proof is the account established and the rite held. Their schools and Essence payoffs are step 5 (ig-m6o.5); departed testimony is step 6.

ARCHITECTURE NOTE 9 (director, v2 Appendix B): testimony against the Ledger. godot-architect owns the split; game-designer owns the volume numbers.
- The Ledger holds settled facts. If every retelling became a record, the 10,000 cap and the records-per-hour estimate would break.
- Keep knowledge and testimony as per-hero state that points into the Ledger.
- Only consequential statements become records: a Herald's covenant, a confession, a public accusation.
- The ig-m6o.9 side file keeps the write cost flat either way.
- Settle it before the full scope after the gate is split. The thin slice (one dream, one bond, one moment) should not need gossip.
2026-09-24 director ruling (GAME_SPEC § 10, folded 2026-09-24): the § 10 PROVISIONAL is settled. Each step-1 piece lands with its first reader, so witnessed details land here with knowledge. The earlier "(GAME_SPEC § 10 PROVISIONAL)" pointer in these notes now means that ruling.

title: Living-world 3: People in combat (bonded chains, informed refusals, rescue motives, recognition)
description:
WHY
New feeling: trust in a particular squad. Relationships change what the squad can do.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction, pillar "People Inside the Fight" and step 3; ruling 3 (Defiance).

SCOPE (tech-lead splits it)
- Finish the skill foundation (the ig-gy0 epic) first. This step builds on it and does not redo it.
- Personal chains across bonded heroes: one commits, and another counters the retaliation. An apprentice answers the missing beat in a grieving survivor's old combo.
- Rescue motives: a bonded hero breaks pursuit, lifts a friend, and casts while carrying.
- Recognition: a veteran recognises a killing pattern it has seen before. The Ledger holds the downed-by moments that make "seen before" true.
- Informed refusals (ruling 3):
  - A hero can refuse or break a mid-fight order.
  - The refusal ALWAYS shows its reason on screen: a bond, a fear or a promise, read from the hero's state and history.
  - It can be right (it saves someone) or tragically wrong.
  - It is never random noise.
  - This amends "per-ability/item Auto or Manual preferences remain authoritative" (GAME_SPEC § Combat model).
- Joy: squad sports, skill exhibitions, apprentices parodying a nemesis's pose.

COMBAT SEAM
Refusal rules live in the one simulation and draw only from its seeded RNG. The forecast must predict refusals exactly as a real run would (boundary #4). A refusal is a moment in the battle record.

DEPENDS
Step 2 (bonds). The ig-gy0 epic (skills).

OPEN (game-designer)
- Refusal frequency and triggers (PROVISIONAL).
- How the player can see a refusal coming.
- Whether a refusal can be overridden, and what that costs.
notes:
2026-09-24 game-designer, OPEN (add to the design): do refusals fire in unwatched repeat runs? A refusal that gets a hero killed while nobody watched reads as a bug, not drama. It also threatens the forecast's safe verdict unless it is fully deterministic in the one simulation. Leaning: refusals fire in watched battles only, or the forecast counts them exactly.
2026-09-24 director clarification: refusals live inside BattleSimulation and draw only seeded RNG, so the forecast stays honest either way. The unwatched-runs question is FEEL (a death nobody saw reads as a bug), not determinism. This supersedes the forecast worry in the note above.
2026-09-24 DIRECTION v2 (final; GAME_SPEC § Direction). Adds to the body above; where it says SUPERSEDES, v2 wins.
V2 STEP 3 LIST: skill eligibility, commitments, reservations, shared technique triggers, Concordance, carrying, recognition and the piloted lens.
- The six personal rules (GAME_SPEC § 6): Trust, Missing beat, Recognition, Commitment, Parliament, Legend. Parliament needs step 6's souls and Legend needs step 4's belief. This step builds the eligibility rule they plug into, not those powers.
- Commitment: a hero rejects an action before spending its cooldown and pursues a stated alternative. Same ruling 3; the body's refusal rules still hold.
- Private techniques [r8]: one can emerge when a deepest commitment is threatened. It fires at the hero's next legal action, respecting cooldowns and the ability lock, and may protect the person you ordered attacked. Witnessing grants knowledge; teaching needs its owner's agreement.
- Rescue [r9]: a persistent objective, reevaluated at each step (separate, reach, lift through the existing carry, extract), never queued blindly. Carrying allows compatible spells and moves; skills that need free hands mean setting the person down. Casting cannot bypass the lift channel.

CONCORDANCE (§ 4; architecture note 6): the sacrifice x3 stays, but it gates on a technique two distinct heroes have practised together, not the same def_id. Kinship can help; rivals can qualify. SYSTEMS § Dupes and resonance carries the Amended line. Open for game-designer: what triggers resonance once the x3 leaves def_id (ig-m6o.4 OPEN).

A2 ITEM ON THIS STEP:
- Offers and responses [r8]. Before a relevant command, a hero states their condition ("I'll cross if Mira covers me"), and the ribbon joins the people and actions involved. Show who waits at whose door, who leaves a seat open, who accepts help. Another hero can visibly contest the piloted hero's reading of the field with a concrete objection; switching lens shows the difference without briefing either hero. Needs step 2's knowledge.

FLAG (sequencing, for the director): v2's Recognition rule is "nemeses predict familiar openings from experience". Across battles that needs a persistent enemy id, and architecture note 1 puts that in the nemesis step (ig-m6o.7). Within one battle it does not. Decide at scoping: either step 3's recognition is within one battle (plus heroes recognising patterns from the Ledger, as the body says), or enemy ids move up to this step.

POINTERS: Held the Bridge's legend skill (ig-m6o.4) and the battlefield band (ig-m6o.5) ride on this step's eligibility rules.
2026-09-24 director ruling (answers the FLAG above; GAME_SPEC § 10): step 3's Recognition works within one battle only. A nemesis or veteran can predict openings it saw earlier in the same fight. Recognition across battles needs persistent enemy ids, and it lands with ig-m6o.7 (architecture note 1). Heroes recognising patterns from the Ledger's downed-by moments (the body's Recognition line) is not affected: heroes already have stable ids. Don't add enemy ids at this step.

title: Town look + camera: pan/zoom over the hex map, grass tint, real hall models
description: From the ig-6m2.1 screenshot (.agent-results/ig-6m2.1/town.png): (1) The overview camera shows only the near hexes and cannot pan, so a 217-hex map (radius 8) is mostly unreachable; add pan (WASD/edge/drag) + zoom, clamped to the map. (2) The hex_grass tiles read lime-yellow under the current light; tint or relight toward a natural green. (3) The seven halls are still grey BoxMesh placeholders; swap them for KayKit hexagon-pack models (credit in CREDITS.md). (4) The Lumbermill crane hides its own label; raise the label. Renderer/view only; no save keys. Visual check via the Godot AI MCP editor_screenshot or a capture script. Coordinate with ig-6m2.2 (halls become placed buildings) so the hall models are done once.

title: Skills 10: balance pass, clear times back in the pre-skill band
description:
WHY
The v1 kits are a large buff (combos alone take sustained damage to about 1.4-1.6x basic swings). Enemy skills offset part of it. This pass puts clear time back where the pre-skill baseline measured it.
Spec: SYSTEMS.md § Skills ("What the kits cost the balance").

SCOPE
- game-designer retunes skill multipliers only: not the six stats, not zone power, not rewards.
- Target: five mixed F-rank level-1 heroes clear Verdant in 72.5-79.0 s over seeds 1 and 2 (the band restated 2026-09-24 after the facing fixes; SYSTEMS.md § Provisional shared combat numbers), and three starter Knights win Verdant bare on seeds 1-4 (today seed 2 times out).
- Class + general check (owner ruling: class plus a shared pool): a C-rank level-30 team of all five classes with full class kits runs Sundered with and without all six general skills each. With them, clear time may fall by at most 10%. Report any change in the forecast safe verdict to the director: general skills add survival, and safe means no downings, so more orders can qualify for unlimited repeats.
- Also check: the forecast safe rate on starter teams does not jump.
- Update SYSTEMS.md § Skills with measured numbers; remove the PROVISIONAL markers the measurements settle.

ACCEPTANCE
Measured clear times in the notes with the log path; BUILT + GUT green.
notes:
2026-09-24 game-designer: target restated (the drift finding from ig-gy0.1's baseline).
- Cause: the only combat-rule commits since the ig-544 measurement are the facing fixes 970856f (ig-oit) and c8b09e2 (ig-hb2). Stats, enemy conversion, zones and kits are unchanged. The heroes/ commits since (callings, passions, keepers, town) leave final battle stats identical. golden_before.json was written 23:51, before the first gy0.1 edit (23:54).
- Old code faced stationary enemies away from the fight, so the Rogue got free rear hits and Flank slots on the near side. That was wrong, and the director ruled it fixed. So the band is RESTATED, not restored: SYSTEMS.md § Provisional shared combat numbers, "Restated 2026-09-24".
- New target: mixed 72.5-79.0 s on seeds 1-2; three Knights win bare on seeds 1-4.
- Knights seed 2 is NOT a stall. At tick 1799, measure:1 cast Rally and revived measure:0, who had been downed by the boss at tick 1798. The boss took its last hit at 1791. The lone final-wave boss (594 HP) was 87% dead bare and 57% dead supplied. The Knights were just slow through waves 1-5. The case sits at the timeout edge (the old top was 173.9/180 s) and swings tens of seconds either way (seed 1 went 173.9 -> 130.3 s). Hence seeds 1-4, not 1-2.
- Fix it here, with the kits, not in a separate pre-skills bead. The kits buff sustained damage 1.4-1.6x and give the Knight new tools. Tuning Knights now means tuning a sim that gy0.2-0.8 are about to change. A timeout is not a loss: living heroes withdraw (SYSTEMS "Timeout withdraws living actors"). A fresh save has no roster, so three Knights is a worst-case summon probe, not the default start.
- One unproven link (optional, one engine run, owner's call): ig-544 measured a working tree that was only committed 37 h later, in 63fd455. Running golden_capture.gd at 63fd455 should reproduce 60.1-65.6. If it does, the facing fixes own the whole drift. If it doesn't, something folded into 63fd455 moved it too.
2026-09-24 director: restatement accepted and SYSTEMS committed. The optional golden_capture run at 63fd455 is SKIPPED on purpose (it doesn't change the call). Don't redo it.
2026-09-24 director, input from ig-gy0.4: the fight changed on purpose. Heroes now counter the enemy ranger and mage 0.8 s telegraphs, every enemy swings its class's starter weaponskill, and enemy Knights carry Crushing Blow (1.2 s, radius 1.5, 2.5x, 14 s). The forecast runs 1.40x slower on verdant5 and 1.14x on frontier50 (high1, median of 5). Measure clear times after gy0.4, not before.
2026-09-24 director finding for game-designer (from ig-gy0.4; code and SYSTEMS disagree at one edge): SYSTEMS § Counters promises a dodge makes a telegraph miss 'if it resolves within 1 s'. The AI answers after skill_reaction_delay_seconds (0.2 s), and Crushing Blow's telegraph is 1.2 s, so the blow resolves exactly 1.0 s after the dodge starts: zero margin. The tick expires statuses before it resolves telegraphs, so on a tie the dodge is already gone. Today the ig-85w late tick makes them tie; tick-exact timers would tie too. The Rogue only survives because the 2 m dash clears the 1.5 radius, so nothing fails in today's game. A line or a bigger circle would hit. Director pick: add margin in the numbers (a 1.2 s dodge on Slip and Dust Roll), not a change to the tick order, which would move every golden. Rule it in this pass, or earlier if a longer or line telegraph lands first.

title: Skills 8: skill books and Training Hall teaching
description:
WHY
The owner ruled skills are also learned from skill books and the Training Hall.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Skills ("Learning"). SYSTEMS.md § Skills (Learning, drop and teach rows). DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Skills" items 3, 11.

BEHAVIOR
1. Books: an extra roll in Expedition.roll_loot's settlement (hub/expedition/expedition.gd) at skill_book_drop_chance per clear (a ZoneDefinition value). It never replaces a stone, part or Essence reward. skill_book_general_share (0.5) of drops are general books, one general skill picked uniformly. The rest are class books for a class book-only skill, class weighted by the roster's archetypes. GameSession.skill_books {skill_id: count}, additive key.
2. Using a book: a GameSession mutator teaches it, adds it to learned_skills, spends the book. A class book needs a hero of its class. A general book needs any hero at or above the skill's tier minimum level (1 / 10 / 20), whatever the hall level. Refused if the hero already knows it. Never another class's skill (owner ruling 2026-09-23).
3. Training Hall teaching, class: a class skill with unlock_level <= hero.level + training_hall_teach_levels_per_level * hall level, for training_hall_teach_parts_per_unlock_level * unlock_level F parts. Never a class book-only skill.
4. Training Hall teaching, general: a general skill whose tier <= hall level and whose minimum level <= hero.level, for training_hall_general_parts[tier] F parts (20 / 40 / 80).
Both add to learned_skills.
5. UI: books in the inventory with a Teach button; a Teach tab in the Training Hall panel with Class and General lists.

ACCEPTANCE
- Spine test: summon stones, parts and Essence from a fixed-seed clear are identical with and without the book roll; compute_essence_yield of a hero is identical before and after it learns skills.
- Disk round-trip of skill_books and learned_skills (boundary #1).
- Tests for every refusal (wrong class, already known, hall too low, hero below a general tier's minimum level, not enough parts, a class book-only skill at the hall, another class's skill).
- About half the book drops over a fixed-seed sample of clears are general.
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass (boundary #1).

NOTE
Touches GameSession save keys and hub panels. Never beside the town lane's save work.
notes:
From the ig-gy0.2 review (nit 5, 2026-09-24): Field Dressing's 'a class heal is ready' check counts a heal on Auto and off cooldown even when it has no valid target, so Field Dressing can hold while nobody heals. Harmless until this bead grants general skills. Before granting them, make 'ready' mean 'ready with a valid target'.
Director ruling 2026-09-24 (from the ig-gy0.2 renames): heroes start at level 0, and EVERY level check reads 0 as 1: skill unlocks (already max(level, 1) at battle_simulation.gd:864), the general tier minimums and hall reach (hero.level + 5 x hall level). Put them all behind one helper, not scattered max() calls.

title: Skills 7: take control of one hero in a watched battle (click + number keys)
description:
WHY
The owner: "players can also take control basically play an mmo character." Thin first version: one hero, watched battles, click and number keys.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Skills ("Take control of one hero"). DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Skills" item 9 (amends the 2026-09-22 "not piloting one hero" line).

BEHAVIOR
1. In a watched battle, select one allied hero and press Take Control (button + hotkey). One piloted hero at a time. Press again or pick another to switch.
2. While piloted, the simulation skips that actor's skill choice and target choice. It auto-attacks its current target. Its chains still run when the player fires a trigger.
3. Right-click ground moves; right-click an enemy targets and attacks (today's commands).
4. A hotbar for the piloted hero: its skills in bar order; keys 1-0 fire the first ten; every skill is clickable (the bar scrolls; no limit). Area skills take a ground click. Cooldowns show on the bar.
5. New command use_skill {actor_id, skill_id, target_id or point}, validated like today's commands (life, range, cooldown, ability lock, silence).
6. Piloted is view state, like tactical pause: cleared on leaving the view and on reload, never saved in the checkpoint, never set in an unwatched run or a forecast.

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests: a piloted actor makes no automatic skill or target choice; use_skill is refused out of range, on cooldown, inside the ability lock and while silenced; a checkpoint saved while piloting has no piloted flag; closing the view returns the hero to AI.
- A played check by the director: take a Knight, stun a Crushing Blow by hand.
- Editable text fields still suppress battle hotkeys.
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass (boundaries #2, #4).

NON-GOALS
WASD, tab-targeting, camera follow, bar pages, rebinding (ig-gy0.8). Owner ruling 2026-09-23: click + number keys first.

title: Skills 6: chains, a trigger skill and what follows, programmed by the player
description:
WHY
The owner: "players should be able to program skill order too, as in theres one trigger skill and the player can choose what skills come after it."
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Skills ("Chains"). SYSTEMS.md § Skills (chain rows). DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: Skills" items 3, 6.

BEHAVIOR
1. Hero.skill_chains: [{trigger, then: [ids]}], at most skill_chain_max_steps after the trigger. One chain per trigger skill. Validated on load (known skills only).
2. In battle: when a trigger fires (AI or player), the actor's chain state starts. The picker's "continue a chain" step fires the next skill as soon as it is ready. A step that cannot fire within skill_chain_step_timeout_seconds is skipped. Counters and revives cut in; the chain resumes after. The chain ends if its target dies or it runs out. Chain state is saved in the checkpoint.
3. A chain is an AI preference. It is not a command queue: a direct order still replaces a direct order.
4. The skill panel gains a chain editor: pick a trigger, then add, remove and reorder the skills after it.

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests: trigger -> steps fire in order; a step on cooldown past the timeout is skipped; a counter cuts in and the chain resumes; target death ends it; a Manual skill inside a chain fires as part of the chain (director ruling 2026-09-23: programming it counts as firing it by hand); an Off skill inside a chain is skipped.
- Disk round-trip of skill_chains, and of a checkpoint mid-chain (boundary #1).
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass (boundaries #1, #4).

NOTE
Touches heroes/hero.gd save keys. Never beside ig-wgj.13, ig-6m2.x save work or ig-gy0.7.
notes: From ig-gy0.3 (2026-09-24): SYSTEMS.md (about line 309) names skill_chain_max_steps, but balance.tres has no such row, so chains have no step cap yet. gy0.3 validates chains (known skills, non-empty 'then') and carries them in the snapshot; nothing reads them until this bead. Add the balance row and the cap here.

title: Town jobs are professions: woodcutting earns XP and a skill bonus (mining, farming as they land)
description:
WHY
The owner ruled (2026-09-23) that the new town jobs are professions too, under the multi-passion system. A worker should get better at its job, and a hero with a woodcutting passion should be the one you want at the Lumbermill.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § The town builder ("Job skills"). Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Keepers and professions ("Workers"). All PROVISIONAL.

BEHAVIOR
1. A worker at a placed workplace earns XP in that workplace's profession (Lumbermill -> woodcutting; Mine and Farm once they exist), on the live tick only, only while home, x passion_xp_multiplier for a passion. Same XP scale as keepers.
2. Output: base_rate * (1 + worker_skill_bonus_per_level * skill). worker_skill_bonus_per_level = 0.10 in balance.tres.
3. The workplace panel shows each worker's skill and whether it has the passion. The assign list sorts passion heroes first.
4. The town script maps workplace type -> profession. No new save keys: profession_xp already holds any profession id.

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests: a home Lumbermill worker earns woodcutting XP (x4 with the passion); an away worker earns none; an offline catch-up grants none; a skill-5 worker makes x1.5 wood.
- A real disk round-trip keeps woodcutting XP.
- BUILT + GUT green. Verifier pass (boundary #1).

NON-GOALS
Masterwork for the town jobs (none: GAME_SPEC.md says skill bonus only); mining and farming buildings (ig-6m2.3.1 adds the Mine, ig-6m2.5.1 the Farm). Whichever lands second adds the map row: if a slice has landed, this bead maps its type; if this bead lands first, that slice adds its one row.
notes:
2026-09-23 game-designer: nothing open.
- Starving (ig-6m2.5) multiplies the final rate after the skill bonus: base * (1 + 0.10*skill) * 0.5.
- A workplace under construction (ig-6m2.3) earns no XP; it has no workers.
- The needs-owner label is removed: the passions ruling (ig-wgj.13) landed.

title: Town builder 6: heroes walk home and to work (replaces ambient wandering)
description:
WHY
The town should look like it works. Heroes in town walk from their House to their job, work there, and walk back. Heroes with no job wander. This covers ig-wgj.7 (keepers stand and work) and replaces ig-wgj.5 (ambient wandering, written for the fixed layout).
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § The town hub ("The town looks alive") and § The town builder. ARCHITECTURE.md § The town is the interface ("Ambient heroes are views onto the roster", "Presentation numbers stay in the view scripts"). DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23 "The town is the interface" (rejected: saving ambient hero positions).

SPLIT (tech-lead, 2026-09-24)
Two slices, in order, one implementer pass each. This parent closes when both close. ig-m6o.2.2 waits on it.
- ig-6m2.6.1, the town works: the hex walk graph, the walker figure, keepers and workers walking House → work spot → House, heroes coming and going, the work clips.
- ig-6m2.6.2, the town lives: heroes with no job wander, the bond partner becomes an ordinary walker (no fixed spot), a click on a walker opens that hero, the wanderer cap with an FPS measurement.

RULES BOTH SLICES KEEP (already ruled)
- Walking is cosmetic (game-designer, 2026-09-23, notes). Production, profession XP and eating never wait for a walk. They follow the saved state (home, station, busy) exactly as ig-6m2.1, .5 and .7 do.
- Nothing is saved: no to_dict/from_dict key, no SaveService change, no GameSession field. Positions and activities are derived and reset on every load.
- TownView never reads GameSession. hub.gd decides who is in town and hands TownView the Hero objects. The view reads hero.station and hero.home, as show_partner already reads hero.home.
- Terms: "in town" = on the roster, not is_hero_busy(), and not the body. "House" = hero.home (GAME_SPEC's "home" means in town).
- Work spots are the WorkSpot Marker3D in each building scene (ig-6m2.2). A House's WorkSpot is its door.
- The work clips come from Rig_Medium_Tools and Rig_Medium_Simulation, staged by ig-wgj.3.
- Presentation numbers are constants in the view scripts, not balance.tres rows (ARCHITECTURE § The town is the interface; rule 9): walk speed, how long a hero works, rests or lingers, the wanderer cap, the clip table.
- Cosmetic randomness uses each walker's own RandomNumberGenerator, seeded from its hero's instance_id. Never the global randi()/randf(): summoning in hub.gd draws from the global RNG, so a view that drew from it would change what the player pulls.

THE WALKABLE AREA (tech-lead ruling, 2026-09-24)
Buildings fill whole hexes, one per hex (TownRules.hex_refusal). A hex is 6 m across the flats, and the biggest building box is 4.5 m. So a hex with no building is open ground, and the walkable area is the hex grid itself.
- TownView keeps an AStar2D (built into Godot) over TownRules.map_hexes: one point per hex centre, joined to its six neighbours. A hex with a building is disabled. show_buildings updates the graph when the set of occupied hexes changes, which is exactly a place or a move.
- A route = start → the centres of the free hexes on the path → end. A segment between two adjacent hex centres stays inside those two hexes, so it never crosses a building (the nearest box edge stays over 1.5 m away).
- A walker enters and leaves a building only through its approach hexes: the building's two neighbours nearest its WorkSpot (with today's markers, the two +z hexes). The last leg, approach-hex centre → WorkSpot, stays clear of the box: the spot sits at local z 2.5 (halls) or 2.8 (House, Lumbermill), and the boxes end at 1.5 and 2.25.
- Free ground = the centre of a map hex with no building. free_point(near) = the free hex centre nearest near. Ties go to the earlier hex in map_hexes order.
- REJECTED: a NavigationRegion3D baked at runtime (an async bake and a new seam, for a grid we already have); steering around boxes with collision (walkers wedge in gaps, and nothing proves they never cut through).

NON-GOALS (both slices)
Schedules, day/night, sleeping animations. Anything saved. Navmesh. Walkers avoiding each other or the body (they may overlap). Walking out to the gate when dispatched (a sent hero just leaves). Summons walking out of the Summoning Circle (they come in through the gate). Pathing for the body's click walk (it stays straight, with its stuck timer). Dialogue beyond the partner's line. Townsfolk who are not on the roster.

FOUND WHILE SCOPING (in neither slice; file separately if wanted)
The body's walk bounds are a fixed square (TownView.WALK_HALF_EXTENT = 23.6 m), but the map has radius 8 (hex (5, 0) is 30 m out). The body cannot reach a building placed that far out: a click on it still opens through the stuck timer, but the body stops at the edge, and a partner standing out there can't be met.
notes:
2026-09-23 game-designer: walking is cosmetic.
- Production, profession XP and eating never wait for a hero to reach its building or its house.
- They follow the saved state (home, station, busy) exactly as in ig-6m2.1, .5 and .7.
- So the walk can change freely without touching a single number or save key.
- The needs-owner label is removed.
2026-09-24 director, from ig-6m2.2: the ig-m6o.2.1 bond partner has no House, so it stands at a fixed spot, BODY_SPAWN + (4, 0, -3) = (4, 0, 2) in town space. That is inside hex (1, 0), the Sanctum's default hex, 0.5 m outside the Sanctum's box. Buildings can move now, and nothing checks that spot, so a House moved onto (1, 0) would swallow the partner. When the partner becomes its ambient hero here, place it by the same free-ground rule as everyone else and drop the fixed spot.

title: Town builder 3: stone, and buildings that take time to go up
description:
WHY
Banished's pull is that building costs material and time. This slice adds the second resource, stone, which pays for hall upgrades (ig-6m2.4). It also makes new buildings take live-play time to go up.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § The town builder. Numbers and rules: SYSTEMS.md § Town builder, "Stone and construction" and "The first of each producer is free" (game-designer ruling 2026-09-23, see the notes; deadlock check 2026-09-24).

RULED (do not reopen)
- One resource, one job. Houses and workplaces cost wood only. Stone pays only for hall upgrades. There is no town_start_stone. This overrides the first scope line, "houses and workplaces cost wood and stone": a stone House needs a Mine, whose workers need Houses, so a fresh town would deadlock.
- The first of each producer is free, and so is the first House (deadlock check, 2026-09-24): from 40 wood, a free Lumbermill plus two more at 20 left 0 wood and no House, with no way back.
- One meaning per model. building_scaffolding and building_stage_A/B/C mean construction only. building_destroyed means a level-0 hall. ig-wgj.6 already carries its new mapping, and this scoping leaves it unchanged.
- Live play only. Stone and build time move in _advance_clocks_in_memory, never in the offline catch-up.
- Halls are never under construction. Hall upgrades stay instant.

SPLIT (tech-lead, 2026-09-24)
Two slices, in order, one implementer pass each. Both touch the save, so both get a boundary #1 review. The parent closes when both close.
- ig-6m2.3.1, Mine and stone: the Mine, stone as a saved resource, the free first House. It unblocks ig-6m2.4, which needs stone but not construction.
- ig-6m2.3.2, construction time: build_remaining, the stage models, and a building under construction does nothing.

ASSETS (no download)
building_mine_blue, building_scaffolding and building_stage_A are in the owner-approved KayKit Medieval Hexagon Pack 1.0 FREE (ig-wgj.3 notes). It is already unzipped at C:\Users\Joony\AppData\Local\Temp\kaykit\town\KayKit_Medieval_Hexagon_Pack_1.0_FREE\Assets\gltf\buildings\ (blue\ and neutral\).
- Copy each .gltf and its .bin flat into hub/town/models/hexagon/.
- They use the hexagons_medieval.png that is already staged.
- If that Temp folder is gone, stop and ask the director: fetching it again is a download.

NON-GOALS
builder jobs (construction just takes time); hauling; food and the Farm (ig-6m2.5); mining XP and skill (ig-6m2.7); hall upgrade costs (ig-6m2.4); demolishing, cancelling or refunding a building; stone costs on anything but hall upgrades; a price or build time for moving.
notes:
2026-09-23 game-designer RULING: the numbers and design calls are set (SYSTEMS.md § Town builder, "Stone and construction"). The tech-lead can finish the body from this.

NUMBERS (balance.tres, PROVISIONAL)
- mine_wood_cost 20
- mine_worker_slots 2
- stone_per_worker_minute 0.5
- house_build_seconds 60
- workplace_build_seconds 120 (Lumbermill, Mine, Farm)

CALLS
1. One resource, one job. Houses and workplaces cost WOOD ONLY. Stone pays only for hall upgrades (ig-6m2.4).
   - This overrides this bead's scope line "houses and workplaces cost wood and stone".
   - Why: a House that costs stone needs a Mine first, and the Mine's workers need Houses, so a fresh town would deadlock without start stone.
   - There is no town_start_stone.
2. The Mine is building_mine_blue from the approved pack, already on disk. Stage it with building_scaffolding and building_stage_A. Those two are not staged yet; stage_B, stage_C and destroyed already are. No new download.
3. The first of each producer is free (SYSTEMS § "The first of each producer is free"). If ig-6m2.1 did not already carry it, it lands here, for the Lumbermill, the Mine and the Farm type key.
4. Construction:
   - A new building shows scaffolding, then stage_A, stage_B and stage_C, a quarter of its build time each, then its own model.
   - Until finished it does nothing. assign_home and station_hero refuse it with a reason, and so do their previews.
   - Its hex is taken. move_building works on it and keeps its progress.
   - It counts as "having one" for the free rule.
5. Saved as the additive key build_remaining (seconds) on the building dict. A missing key means finished, so every ig-6m2.1/.2 building loads finished.
6. Build time moves only in _advance_clocks_in_memory. The offline catch-up moves it 0.
7. The halls are never under construction. Hall upgrades stay instant.
8. One meaning per model: scaffolding and stage_A/B/C mean construction only; destroyed means a level-0 hall. ig-wgj.6 has its new mapping.

ACCEPTANCE ADDS
- A half-built building survives a real disk save and reload with its build_remaining.
- An old save loads with every building finished.
- A building under construction refuses a resident and a worker.
- Build time moves on the live tick at 1 s per s, and 0 across an offline catch-up of any length.
- Free rule: with none, 0; with one under construction, full price; preview equals result.
- A Mine worker makes stone at the table rate only while home.
The needs-owner label is removed.

title: Town builder 4: hall upgrades also cost wood and stone
description:
WHY
The town has to feed the hero game, or it is a side game. The link is the halls: upgrading the Circle, Forge, Training Hall, Sanctum or Reliquary now also costs wood and stone, on top of today's parts.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § The town builder ("What the town makes, and what it pays for"). Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Town builder, "Hall upgrades cost wood and stone" (game-designer ruling 2026-09-23, see the notes; PROVISIONAL until played).

RULED (do not reopen)
- Going from level n to n+1 costs 20·(n+1) wood and 10·(n+1) stone, on top of the unchanged 10·(n+2) rank-n parts. n is the current level. A hall costs 300 wood and 150 stone in total.
- The parts cost stays. It is calibrated against the spine (264 clears to max one hall).
- Levels already reached stay. Nothing is refunded or charged again.
- This applies only to the five halls with levels. The Apothecary and the Town Gate have none.
- Upgrades stay instant: halls are never under construction.
- This changes today's game on purpose: a player with no Mine cannot upgrade a hall.

BEHAVIOR
1. The plan. _building_upgrade_plan also takes the town's wood and stone, and returns wood_cost and stone_cost next to part_rank and part_cost. Both are computed there, next to the parts formula, from two new rows. No other file derives a cost.
2. It is valid only when parts, wood and stone are all enough. The error names every resource that is short, and only those: "Need 30 D parts (have 12) and 20 stone (have 0)."
3. upgrade_building spends all three, or nothing.
4. preview_building_upgrade passes GameSession.town_resources. upgrade_building builds the same plan, so the preview equals the result.
5. Hub.
   - The level row reads "Forge — Lv 1 · Next 30 D parts · 40 wood · 20 stone". MAX is unchanged.
   - _upgrade_building takes the preview before it upgrades. Its success line reads the costs from that plan, and its refusal line shows the plan's error.
   - hub.gd stops working out 10·(level+2) itself. Today it does, in both of those lines.
6. Numbers. Add hall_upgrade_wood_per_level 20 and hall_upgrade_stone_per_level 10 to balance_table.gd and balance.tres. Keep other people's uncommitted work in both files intact.

SAVE (boundary #1)
- No new key. Wood and stone already save in town_resources (ig-6m2.1 and ig-6m2.3.1), and building_levels doesn't change.
- An existing save with hall levels loads unchanged.
- ig-6pm: nothing new to repair or refuse.

ACCEPTANCE (tests/unit, APPDATA redirected)
- At each n from 0 to 4:

title: Ambient life: home heroes wander and use stalls (never saved)
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-23: "we see our heros walking around, interacting with stalls and shops, and make it seem alive". Heroes who are home should be visible in town, doing small things. See ARCHITECTURE.md § The town is the interface: ambient heroes are views derived from the roster and are never saved.

1. Show up to AMBIENT_HERO_CAP heroes who are home: on the roster, not busy (is_hero_busy), and not the body. Pick order: favorites, then higher rank, then lower instance_id. The order is stable, so the same heroes appear each visit.

4. Refresh on roster_changed and expeditions_changed:
   - a dispatched hero leaves
   - a returning hero appears
   - a killed hero vanishes

Measure the FPS with the cap at 8, 12 and 16 on the owner's machine. Set AMBIENT_HERO_CAP to the highest value that holds 60 FPS, and mark it PROVISIONAL in the code comment and the bead notes.

ACCEPTANCE

  - the set updates after a dispatch, a return and a kill_hero
  - to_dict() is identical before and after ambient heroes spawn
