title: Squad battle readability after KayKit swap: faction ring, corpse cue, cleric silhouette
description:
Design follow-up from the ig-ixj review (Opus::extra 1 game, 2026-09-23). The KayKit swap removed ALLY_COLOR/ENEMY_COLOR tint and DEAD_COLOR, which were the only faction and death cues on the old capsules.

Evidence: .agent-results/ig-ixj/battle_live.png (melee clump). Wide shots separate by palette, but a clump does not: crimson Skeleton_Mage hats sit next to purple hero Mage hats, and 10 dead skeletons look like 5 live ones.

Issues:
1. Faction cue: reviewer suggests a thin faction-coloured ground ring under every unit, reusing the selection-ring TorusMesh with 2 shared static materials (no per-unit material copies).
2. Corpse cue: a shared static material_overlay dim on dead units, or sink and hide corpses once the death clip ends.
3. Cleric reads as Mage (same model, wand vs staff only), so the healer is invisible at battle zoom. PROVISIONAL mapping from ig-ixj.
4. Cosmetic: Skeletons_Death hips slide about 0.85 world units back after the root pin (hips track kept on purpose), plus the fling, so corpses land 1.1-1.65 units from the sim spot.

Route: game-designer picks the cues, then implementer. Renderer only (combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd). No sim changes. Perf: ig-ixj already costs about 1.9x render median at 60 units, so every cue must use shared materials.
notes:
Items 1+2 done per director ruling (2026-09-23), renderer only (combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd), sim untouched. (1) Faction ring: thin flattened TorusMesh (r 0.49-0.55, y-scale 0.3) under every unit, inside the gold selection ring. One static mesh plus 2 static unshaded materials: ALLY_COLOR a8c9a8 and ENEMY_COLOR e87b68, the old capsule colors from da554c1^ (director: keep green/salmon, matches the HP bars). Hidden on dead, shown on downed. (2) Corpse cue: static 50%-black material_overlay (CORPSE_DIM) on a dead unit's meshes. The killing-hit flash keeps the overlay until it ends, then _clear_flash hands over to the dim. Both are marked PROVISIONAL (ig-hpu) in code, settled by a played build. Tests: test_every_unit_stands_on_a_shared_faction_ring_until_it_dies, test_the_killing_hit_flashes_before_the_corpse_dims, and _assert_dead_look now checks ring hidden + dim. Mutation 6/6 killed (.agent-results/ig-hpu/mutation.txt). Perf at 60 units (fallen_citadel, benchmark.gd from ig-ixj): render median before 3.385/3.284 ms, after 3.325/3.464 ms. +2%, inside run-to-run noise. Still about 1.8x the old 1.9 ms capsule baseline, no new cost. Screenshots before_/after_{wide,clump,corpses}.png, compare_corpses.png (corpse region about 25% darker). BUILT: gate exit 0, 0 errors/0 warnings; GUT 474/474. Godot procs 0. Not staged. Items 3 (Cleric silhouette) and 4 (Skeletons_Death hip slide) stay open: label needs-design.
2026-09-23 director: items 1+2 committed; CORPSE_DIM alpha 0.5 -> 0.7 (50% was barely visible in compare_corpses.png). Items 3 (cleric silhouette) and 4 (hip slide) remain, needs-design; cleric look folds into the skill-system design.
2026-09-23 game-designer RULING, items 3+4 (build without asking). Renderer only, no sim change. Files: heroes/hero_model.gd, combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd, tests/unit/test_battle_unit_view.gd. Measurements below come from the GLBs (python parse, no Godot).

ITEM 3: CLERIC CUE = HAT OFF + HALO. Not folded into ig-4if: the Cleric must read while idle too (Mend is on an 8 s cooldown), so the static cue lives here.
Why: Mage.glb's Mage_Hat is its own skinned mesh, and it is the Mage's whole top-down read. Its brim is 1.86 x 1.97 model units, wider than the head (1.14) and the body (0.86). title: Combat punch pack: hit-stop, lunge, squash, corpse fling, last-kill slow-mo, compact health bars
description: Owner picks 2026-09-23 (ideas 2,4,5,6,7) plus small health bars that don't clutter. View-only. The sim, snapshot and saves are untouched. Full spec in notes.

notes:
DISPATCH BRIEF (director, 2026-09-23). View-only. No creative work beyond this; ask instead.
FILES: combat/battle/battle_unit_view.gd, combat/battle/battle_view.gd, combat/battle/battle_vfx.gd, tests/unit/test_battle_unit_view.gd, tests/unit/test_battle_vfx.gd. Nothing else. NEVER touch battle_simulation.gd, battle_actor.gd, battle_state.gd, saves, .tscn, project.godot.
BUILDS ON ig-0gt (crit tick, red/yellow numbers, recoil on pivot x/z). Read its final code first.

OFFSETS RULE: recoil, lunge and fling all move the pivot on x/z. Keep a separate Vector3 offset per effect and set pivot.position = their sum (plus the death lift on y) in one place. No two tweens may write pivot.position directly.

2 HIT-STOP: on a hit event with critical=true, freeze the target's view animation (lerp + its tweens) for 0.06s. If a basic_attack event in the same render targets it, freeze that attacker too. Non-crit hits: no freeze.
4 LUNGE: on a basic_attack event where the attacker's archetype is not ranger/mage: lunge offset 0.3 toward the target over 0.07s, back to 0 over 0.15s (ease-out).
5 SQUASH: on a hit: pivot scale (1.15, 0.85, 1.15) back to ONE over 0.12s. On a crit: (1.25, 0.75, 1.25). Not on dead units once the death pose has started.
6 CORPSE FLING: on life alive->dead: fling offset slides along -facing during the 0.35s tip-over, 0.8 units if last_crit_tick advanced in that render, else 0.25, plus a small y arc peaking at 0.3. It must end at rest. A first-sight dead unit snaps (no fling).
7 LAST-KILL SLOW-MO: when a render takes the living enemy count from >0 to 0, the battle VIEW runs at 0.35x for 0.4s of real time. That covers unit lerps and every tween in units and vfx. NEVER use Engine.time_scale (it slows GameSession clocks for every expedition). NEVER scale the delta passed to BattleSimulation.advance in practice mode.
HEALTH BARS (replaces the current _hp_fill box):
- Billboarded, unshaded, drawn over geometry (no depth test) so bodies never hide it. Centered at y 2.2. 0.7 wide x 0.07 tall. Enemies with elite: 0.85 wide.
- Layers: a background 1a1a1a at alpha 0.6; a trailing damage chip f5e6a8 that eases down to the new value over 0.4s after a hit; a fill 6fcf6f for allies / e8483c for enemies.
- Visibility, to cut clutter: shown when hp < max_hp OR selected. Hidden at full hp. Hidden when dead. Hidden when downed (the downed marker covers that case).
- Heals: the fill rises immediately and the chip snaps to it.
TESTS: each effect's trigger and non-trigger case, the offsets-sum rule (a recoil during a lunge ends at zero), bar visibility rules, the chip trailing behavior (Tween.custom_step, no wall-clock waits), and slow-mo leaves the practice sim delta untouched.

title: Flaky GUT: one-off 'Save v3 is invalid: Battle actor archetype or faction is invalid'
description: Seen once, 2026-09-23, by Opus::high 1 game during ig-r9y: 1 of 4 full GUT runs went 312/313 with an unexpected push_error 'Save v3 is invalid: Battle actor archetype or faction is invalid' in a non-view test. Test name not captured. Director rerun: 313/313. A flake in a save-validation path is a boundary-1 (save round-trip) smell: likely order-dependent state or RNG-dependent actor generation hitting an invalid archetype/faction. Next: loop the suite (or tests/unit/test_battle_persistence.gd + test_save_service.gd) until it reproduces, capture the test name and seed.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduced with test name, or root-caused from code; fix lands with a test that fails deterministically before the fix.
notes:
2026-09-23 investigation (Opus::high 1), no repo edits.
MEASURED: deterministic repro with a scratch probe (-s script outside repo, APPDATA redirected to %TEMP%/ig8lj_appdata): knight dispatched via dispatch_force -> save() true -> load_game() true. Cleric same path -> save() true -> load_game() false, load_blocked, 'Save v3 is invalid: Battle actor archetype or faction is invalid.'
ROOT CAUSE (READ): combat/battle/battle_actor.gd:9 VALID_ARCHETYPES = knight/ranger/mage/rogue. Cleric is a real hero (heroes/defs/cleric.tres, docs/SYSTEMS.md five archetypes) and Summon rolls it 1 in 5 (hub/summon/summon.gd:5,26). game_session.gd:772 copies hero.def_id into the actor archetype. Nothing blocks a cleric at dispatch, and the sim tolerates it (battle_simulation.gd:783 ABILITIES.has guard). Only the load validator rejects it. Production impact: any player who sends a cleric to battle writes a save the next boot refuses. load_blocked then also blocks every later save().
FLAKE MECHANISM (INFERRED, not reproduced): the failing test was test_save_service.gd test_missing_save_is_refused_without_error (only assert_push_error_count(0) in the suite, and GUT printed 'Expected 0 push_error errors. Got 1' + Unexpected Errors). That test deletes user://save.json and then loads, so in-process it cannot see a file. The GUT command does not redirect APPDATA, so every GUT/game run shares %APPDATA%/Godot/app_userdata/Infinite Gacha/save.json. Godot logs show other GUT runs with 328 tests (not this tree's 313) at 15:51 and 15:52, during this engine-ownership window. A concurrent writer holding a cleric battle is the only path that fits. Did not loop 15 runs: a serial loop cannot hit a cross-process race, and running two Godot processes breaks the serialize rule.
Proposed fix awaiting director approval (boundary 1). Get-Process Godot* empty.

title: Playtest timed expedition and recovery pacing
description:
## Objective
Determine whether the provisional timed expedition and active recovery pacing makes building multiple teams and recovering lost gear practical in a played session.

## Existing context
ig-6l4 implements concurrent reserved teams, finite and safe repeat orders, automatic rewards, and bulk management. docs/SYSTEMS.md defines base seconds 60/180/300, five-hero floors 15/45/75, square-root strength scaling, and the 5/team_size workload factor. Recovery uses 900 + 300*Reliquary active seconds and pauses on new losses. Automated formula examples are not playtest evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
Record a fresh three-pull save progressing to its second viable team; compare one geared squad with several squads; play a lost-gear recovery scenario with a surviving weak roster at low and high Reliquary levels. Record roster/gear, destinations, elapsed active time, income, idle periods, and decisions. Give an evidence-backed keep/change recommendation for the director. Do not change balance during the measurement. If later balance changes are authorized, run powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests\import_gate.ps1 and the full unit suite on that final state.

## Files allowed to change
.agent-results/ig-6l4-pacing/ evidence only; this Bead's notes. Production balance/spec edits need a separately accepted decision.

## Non-goals
No stamina, paid timers, new currencies, offline repeat chains, permadeath redesign, combat controls, or automatic destructive processing.

title: Timed expeditions, team presets, and bulk management
description:
Objective: replace click-speed expedition farming with concurrent timed dispatches so roster depth and equipped strength improve sustained returns. The user explicitly requested timers, named team presets, send-X-times/auto-repeat, and bulk resource management. This is Astra's proposed direction pending user decisions and a decision-complete Plan-mode specification; it is not an accepted implementation plan.

Each hero may participate in one active expedition. Separate teams run concurrently without an energy meter or arbitrary small dispatch cap. Equipped heroes and their gear are reserved while away, with no mid-run transfers or sacrifice. Show duration before dispatch; derive it from current team strength against mission difficulty with diminishing gains and a nonzero floor. Exact timing and reward tuning are provisional and must cover a fresh save with only three pulls and compare solo with full-team efficiency because current enemies scale with team size.

Preserve combat and permadeath: a past clear is history, not proof of safety. Derive any Safe label from conservative worst-case attrition for the current roster, gear, and zone, including retreat threshold, and validate it before trusting it. Named presets require durable hero identities rather than names or indices, show missing or busy members, and never silently substitute. Preset launch offers one run, a finite total run count, and eventually until-stopped looping. Repeat orders recheck availability and safety, stop on casualty, retreat, or an incomplete team, and support stop-after-current-run. Credit rewards automatically. A dispatch board shows team, zone, remaining time, completed/ordered runs, and cumulative rewards, with collectable reports for review.

Clock behavior awaits the user's async answer. Astra's proposed default is that dispatched missions finish while closed while repeats run only while open; alternatives are session-only timing or bounded repeats progressing offline. Do not assume an answer.

Recovery remains unresolved. The current global expedition-turn clock would let parallel or automatic returns rapidly expire lost gear. Before implementation, explicitly redesign expiry and damage aging while preserving a meaningful Reliquary benefit; do not silently retain or replace the existing rule.

Bulk QoL reuses existing batch salvage/sacrifice and filters. Add protection for favorites, preset members, away heroes, and equipped gear; selection by rank, type, slot, and availability; clear destructive previews with outputs; quantity/all-eligible salvage and sacrifice; and batch part conversion with a keep-at-least reserve. The user's word refine is ambiguous among salvage, part conversion, and enhancement; identify the intended meaning before creating any resource system. No automatic destructive processing by default.

Scope implementation only after design acceptance: (1) timed persisted dispatch, reservations, presets, and finite repeats as one complete player loop; (2) richer bulk management and advanced automation. Existing ig-544 (controlled playable expeditions) and ig-yzc (hop into a sent run) are related direction, but neither grants scope for this work and neither is changed by this epic.

Technical entry points are hub/hub.gd:_on_expedition_pressed/_do_expedition, hub/expedition/expedition.gd:resolve, systems/game_session.gd, systems/save_service.gd, and heroes/hero.gd. Saves are version 1 with no durable hero IDs or migration machinery, and current resolution performs multiple automatic saves. Design exactly-once rewards and casualties, deterministic restart behavior, version-1 migration, and stable completion ordering for concurrent returns. Keep the three-autoload cap, central kill_hero path, and SaveService ownership. Change the explicit no-clock/no-offline-accrual spec only through an accepted plan. In Default mode, do not implement this complex epic until a decision-complete Plan-mode plan is accepted or the user explicitly overrides that gate.

Eventual acceptance: run tests/import_gate.ps1 and the full GUT suite; add focused reservation, repeat, timer, and migration tests plus actual isolated-APPDATA save/reload checks for in-flight missions, duplicate-return prevention, and old saves; visually check populated and empty dispatch boards. Do not mutate the user's save, run concurrent Godot processes, or perform git operations, commits, or pushes. This design/source-inspection turn establishes no runtime proof.
notes:
ACCEPTED DESIGN — 2026-09-21 (user authorized implement-all; direct authorization governs proceeding)

Entry point: core worker starts at systems/game_session.gd + systems/save_service.gd, then deterministic combat/expedition rules and serialization. UI worker separately owns hub/hub.gd, hub/hub.tscn, theme/UI tests and docs; core worker must not edit those paths. Do not close this epic until all core, UI, verification, save/reload, and review gates are complete.

1. Identity/schema: Save version 2. Hero and Item gain stable random serialized instance_id:String and favorite:bool=false. Legacy v1 missing IDs migrate once. Names and indices are never identity. Persist GameSession team_presets:Array[Dictionary], expedition_orders:Array[Dictionary], expedition_reports:Array[Dictionary], recovery_clock_seconds:float, recovery_clock_paused:bool. Presets are {id,name,hero_ids:Array[String],zone_id}; preserve missing/dead references and never substitute. At the v2 trust boundary reject duplicate object IDs, malformed presets/orders, duplicate/invalid teams, unknown/locked dispatch zones, overlapping active teams, invalid finite/count/time/seed state, and do not overwrite canonical save on rejection.

2. Reservations/protection: one hero may be in at most one active order; unlimited disjoint orders. Shared backend guards prevent busy heroes from equip/unequip/rank-up/sacrifice/recovery/arena availability and prevent touching busy equipped gear. kill_hero remains the only roster removal path and must remain usable for expedition deaths; sacrifice guard precedes it. Preset/favorite membership protects heroes from destructive sacrifice; favorite/equipped items protect bulk salvage. Non-destructive equip/enhance remains allowed for non-busy favorites. Revalidate at commit.

3. Timing: combat_ratio=Hero.compute_team_power(team)/(zone.recommended_power*team.size()/5.0). full_team_seconds=max(zone.minimum_duration_seconds,zone.base_duration_seconds/sqrt(combat_ratio)); actual_seconds=ceil(full_team_seconds*5.0/team.size()). Reject empty/invalid/zero-power teams. Author Verdant 60/15, Ashfall 180/45, Sundered 300/75 seconds. Values are provisional pending play; do not alter current reward/combat tuning. Verify equal-gear 1-vs-5 throughput and fresh-three-hero pace.

4. Safety/repeats: forecast emulates worst-case loss damage across Wave.from_zone using exact max HP, rounding, cumulative HP, and non-boss <=25% retreat rule including all traits/stats. Safe only if every hero survives every wave and no retreat. Finite risky dispatch allowed with warning; infinite requires safe and rechecks before every repeat. total_runs is 1..999 including initial; 0 means infinite. Automatically bank every completed run and track cumulative stones/xp/items and runs_completed. Stop after casualty, retreat/failure, incomplete team, or stop_requested; stop means finish current. Captured membership/destination are immutable under preset edits.

5. Clock: persist per-order stable ID, deterministic run seed, initial duration and remaining_seconds. Use monotonic online delta; persist saved_at_unix for offline elapsed max(0, now-saved_at_unix). On load subtract offline time only from already-dispatched current runs; resolve each due run once, then start at most the next repeat at full duration in the open session. No recursive offline catch-up. Rollback gives zero offline progress; forward jump completes current run only. Stable due ordering is remaining time then order ID. Pulse about 0.25s; no per-frame save. Periodic timer/recovery save about 15s and durable dispatch/completion mutations. Pause-menu pause stops online delta; closing follows offline rule. UI observes backend scheduling and need not own it.

6. Exactly once: persisted seed drives deterministic local RNG through expedition/quick-resolve while preserving public resolve(team,wave) seam via helper/optional expedition entry. Defer existing signal-triggered saves during resolution and commit one atomic save containing casualties, cache, rewards, order advance, report. Atomic failure restores pre-transaction memory, preserves previous canonical save, sets notice, and cannot retry awards from mutated memory. Dispatch has the same durability. SaveService remains sole file owner; prevent from_dict/load autosave recursion and preserve newer-version refusal. Add actual isolated-APPDATA reload tests.

7. Recovery: turns remains historical completed/attempted expedition count only. Cache expiry moves to an active recovery clock that runs only in unpaused, active gameplay and never offline. Any new cache pauses recovery_clock_paused. acknowledge_recovery_losses unpauses all current losses. Cache stores its created recovery-clock value. Lifetime seconds=900+300*ReliquaryLevel; damage age converts elapsed active seconds to minutes and reuses 0.03 per unit, Reliquary -0.03/level, and power penalty. Preserve strict <0 expiration. Legacy turn age maps to elapsed active minutes while preserving remaining effective window and migrated caches start paused. Parallel returns/dispatch do not age caches. Recovery acknowledgment is independent from report retention.

8. Reports: retain newest 50. Each summarizes captured team/zone, outcome, casualty names, per-run and cumulative rewards, and stop reason. Rewards never depend on review.

Public backend API: GameSession.hero_by_id(id:String)->Hero; is_hero_busy(hero:Hero)->bool; is_hero_protected(hero:Hero)->bool; is_item_protected(item:Item)->bool; set_hero_favorite(hero:Hero,value:bool)->void; set_item_favorite(item:Item,value:bool)->void; save_team_preset(preset_id:String,preset_name:String,hero_ids:Array[String],zone_id:String)->String; delete_team_preset(id:String)->bool; dispatch_expedition(hero_ids:Array[String],zone_id:String,total_runs:int,team_name:String,preset_id:String='')->String; request_stop_expedition(order_id:String)->void; acknowledge_recovery_losses()->void. ExpeditionOrders.duration_seconds(team:Array[Hero],zone:ZoneDefinition,balance:BalanceTable)->float; safety_forecast(...)->Dictionary {safe:bool,reason:String}. Add `expeditions_changed` for timer/order UI refresh, separate from autosave roster_changed, plus explicit testable tick/offline entry points. Bulk API follows as a separate exact handoff; do not guess it.

Core ownership: heroes/hero.gd, equipment/item.gd, equipment/lost_cache.gd, combat/quick_resolve.gd, hub/expedition/expedition.gd, new hub/expedition/expedition_orders.gd, systems/game_session.gd, systems/save_service.gd, balance_table.gd, balance.tres, zones/zone_definition.gd and three zone definitions as needed, new systems/bulk_operations.gd, backend tests/unit and tests/save_roundtrip_check.gd. No hub UI/docs/tool/.godot/manual uid edits. No engine until director grants exclusive slot; no git or user-save access.
ACCEPTED BULK SCOPE — 2026-09-22

Refining means batch operations over the existing salvage, sacrifice, enhancement and part-conversion systems; no new resource system. Public API: GameSession.preview_bulk_salvage(item_ids:Array[String],quantity:int)->Dictionary; preview_bulk_sacrifice(hero_ids:Array[String],target_id:String,quantity:int)->Dictionary; preview_bulk_enhance(item_ids:Array[String],target_level:int,budget_parts:Array[int])->Dictionary; preview_bulk_conversion(rank:int,quantity:int,reserve:int)->Dictionary; commit_bulk_plan(plan:Dictionary)->bool. quantity=0 means all eligible/max convertible; positive is a deterministic exact limit. last_action_error:String is ephemeral.

Plans are read-only dictionaries with shared keys kind, valid, error, entries, excluded, cost_parts[8], gain_parts[8], essence_gain, resonance_gain, parameters. Entries carry stable IDs, names, rank and operation-specific before/after/spend/gain fields; excluded entries carry id/name/reason. Commit rebuilds from the current profile and refuses any stale eligibility, protection, membership, cost/output, Forge, target, gear, rank or resource change. One SaveService-backed memory/disk transaction commits the whole batch or rolls it all back on write failure. No generic action/plugin framework.

All pure selection/arithmetic lives in new static res://hub/bulk_operations.gd; GameSession supplies profile state and applies coordinated mutations. Reuse the existing single-item formulas. Salvage/sacrifice exclude favorites, preset members, busy heroes, equipped gear/fodder; sacrifice excludes recipient. Selected/displayed order is deterministic and quantity never fills from unselected resources. Preview exact parts/essence/resonance.

Enhancement permits favorite inventory items, bounds target by current Forge cap, accepts eight nonnegative per-rank budgets also capped by actual parts, and processes each selected item to target before the next. Skip target <= current with reason. No random/new enhancement mechanic. Conversion accepts source ranks 0..6, preserves reserve, computes max=floor(max(0,parts[rank]-reserve)/3), refuses positive quantity above max, spends 3 per output, and never cascades. Add focused backend tests for protection, stale plans, funds, budget/reserve and atomic failure.

Architecture correction: systems/ remains reserved for the three autoloads, so BulkOperations is hub/bulk_operations.gd. Duration settings remain ZoneDefinition fields; shared recovery settings live in balance.tres.
CORE MILESTONE CHECKPOINT — 2026-09-22 (SOURCE DRAFT, UNVERIFIED)
Implemented v2 identity/favorite/profile schema, strict pre-mutation v2 validation, v1 identity/recovery migration, blocked-load/write refusal state, staged save bool result, memory rollback transaction coordination, persisted seeded timed orders, stable due ordering, one-current-run offline progress, active-only recovery clock, deterministic reports/repeats/stops, duration/safety rules, busy/protection guards, and pure bulk previews/atomic stale-plan commits. UI API/schema sent to expedition_ui. No engine or save-path runtime evidence yet; required tests and gates remain. Initial edited core files have SHA256 pre-edit hashes but no byte-copy baseline; untouched SaveService/tests were copied before edit under .agent-results/ig-6l4/baseline. Epic remains in_progress.

title: Determinism: full-precision floats in saves; tick-exact timers
description:
WHY
Two pre-existing numeric shortcuts surfaced in the ig-gy0.2 review (high1, 2026-09-24, nits 6 and 7):
1. SaveService writes floats at JSON default precision, so a battle reloaded from a checkpoint drifts about 1e-12 HP from one never saved. A tie on equal HP could break differently after a reload. Likely root-cause fix: JSON.stringify(..., full_precision = true) in SaveService, one argument; old saves still load. Verify the Godot 4.7 signature first.
2. Timers add 0.1 s ticks with no epsilon, so a 1.0 s lock or delay clears on the 11th tick (+10%), and an 8 s cooldown takes 81 ticks. Fix it in one place: count integer ticks, or compare with an epsilon.

ACCEPTANCE
- A checkpoint reloaded through disk finishes bit-identical to the unsaved battle. Tighten the gy0.2 persistence test from 'as written' to exact.
- A 1.0 s lock clears on tick 10.
- The goldens are re-baselined on purpose (the timer fix changes them), and the diff is reviewed.
- BUILT green. Boundary #1 review (Sol).
notes: 2026-09-24 (high1, ig-gy0.4): the same tick residue delays telegraphs. A 1.2 s telegraph lands at 1.3 s, and 0.8 s at 0.9 s. gy0.4's tests allow for the extra tick, so tighten them when this lands. gy0.4 re-baselined the pre-skills checkpoint golden (test_battle_persistence) because counters and enemy kits change that fight on purpose. This fix re-baselines it again.

title: Living-world 7: Fate becomes an opponent (Guests, nemeses, stolen names, Door overthrow, the chair)
description:
WHY
New feeling: rivalry with a world that knows you. Fate has a face.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction, pillar "Fate Has a Face" and step 7; rulings 3 and 5.

SCOPE (tech-lead splits it)
- Selectable Guests: Mother Briar (tangled affections), the Gilded Jackal (outrageous wagers), Sister Cinder (unfinished promises).
- Causal schemes built from the player's real Ledger history. Omens you can read and bargain over. You can discover the causal chain behind an encounter.
- Evolving nemeses: named and scarred, they remember your tactics and may retire to teach counters. Enemies need a stable identity here, and the Ledger's "enemy:<archetype>" becomes a real id.
- Stolen names: recover one through the habits and techniques its forgotten owner left behind.
- Door overthrow (ruling 3): your own heroes can overthrow you, the Door. It is rare and earned, never random. The trigger reads the Ledger (a long record of how you used your people).
- The chair challenge (ruling 5): only a Risen hero (F->SSS by deeds, step 4) can steal the Guest's chair. A hero born above F cannot.

DEPENDS
Step 6.

OPEN
- What happens to the town after an overthrow. Proposal: that town "falls" and enters the Old World (step 8).
- The Guest selection UI.
- Nemesis save identity (needs an ADR).
notes:
2026-09-24 game-designer, OPEN (add to the design): Door overthrow follows the hard constraint that the town never kills while the game is closed. An overthrow resolves only on the live clock, and is warned first, like starvation.
2026-09-24 DIRECTION v2 (final; GAME_SPEC § Direction). Adds to the body above; where it says SUPERSEDES, v2 wins.
V2 STEP 7 LIST: feasible encounter generation, dream collisions, Guest priorities, wagers, nemesis careers, stolen names and chair succession.
- The Guest arranges feasible opportunities; the chorus only influences who answers within the rolled rank. Neither replaces the pity traveler [r9].
- Chair succession [r5, r9]: a living Risen contests the chair by resolving a scheme through their own counter-plan and winning the support of the people affected. The seat is taken in a public reckoning, and the former hero becomes a Guest. That removes a living hero, so it needs note 2's departure path (ig-m6o.5).
- Enemies promote through recorded events, learn, inherit, retire and found schools. Their authored chronicles can be mistaken, and exploited.

ARCHITECTURE NOTE 1: the nemesis step must give every spawned enemy a persistent id before it matters, and promotion reveals it. The v1 Ledger is unaffected: no enemy survives from one battle to the next today. See the recognition flag on ig-m6o.3.
ARCHITECTURE NOTE 3: the Door's anchor is the Summoning Circle building. Hunted, captured and rescued need it to be a real place on the town grid, and it is not yet: the Hall hexes are fixed.

A2 ITEMS ON THIS STEP:
1. The Door has a body [r3].
   - Loved: residents who repeatedly see the Door keep promises that matter to them start a covenant and volunteer anchors, guards or service. They build a public house around the threshold, with a place for every household.
   - Hunted: survivors or messengers carry evidence of where you are. Enemies pursue the anchor and fasten siege gear to it. A captured anchor limits where you open and whom they let through. Defend, relocate, misdirect or bargain.
   - Rescued: if the anchor is captured, free people with a commitment to you mount a liberation expedition from their own allies and resources. You command or pilot willing rescuers under their own commitments. Someone you once saved breaks in carrying your old household banner.
   - Overthrown: an informed coalition forms around a grievance, gains backing across institutions and physically seizes the anchor. It imposes a binding covenant, confinement or expulsion into the next chapter (ig-m6o.8). Your own streets become its approach routes. The old town persists as an independent homeland, and its people carry their accounts of you. The existing note still holds: an overthrow resolves only on the live clock, and is warned first.
2. Killing their leader changes people [r2].
   - Witnessed succession: witnesses react first; distant fighters learn through runners, shouts and officers. Loyalists try to recover, rivals contest command, conscripts try to escape, each by their own relationships. Find who really holds the formation together.
   - The surviving apprentice keeps their kit and what they saw of your victory, rebuilds around that lesson and may replace the mentor's doctrine.
   - The enemy's missing beat: two survivors complete their dead leader's famous formation with a new partner.
2026-09-24 director ruling (GAME_SPEC § 10): recognition across battles lands HERE, with architecture note 1's persistent enemy ids. Step 3 (ig-m6o.3) builds Recognition within one battle only. When this step gives enemies ids, extend Recognition to "seen in an earlier battle". Plan for that reader when scoping the id.

title: Living-world 8: History becomes spectacle (the Founder walks, the Town gets up, the Old World)
description:
WHY
New feeling: astonishment at what these lives built. History becomes spectacle.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction, step 8; ruling 1 (the Old World).

SCOPE (tech-lead splits it)
- The Founder Walks Again: a retiree's pupils and institutions combine into one legendary formation for one battle.
- The Town Gets Up: pilot the town itself to rescue an expedition.
- The homeland congress: homeland societies contest the Door's future.
- The Old World (ruling 1: runs stack up). A fallen or retired town becomes a homeland rift for the next town.
  - Your champion can return as a future nemesis.
  - A chair-thief becomes the next town's Guest.
  - The old town's living people become that rift's population.
  - The dead never return (ruling 4).

AMENDMENT
This ends "one roster forever" and "no run structure" (GAME_SPEC § Win and loss, amended).

DEPENDS
Step 7.

OPEN (owner and game-designer, before tech-lead splits it)
- What "fallen" means. Proposal: overthrown (step 7), or the roster lost with no way back.
- Whether retiring is a menu choice and what it costs.
- Whether the Ledger carries over (proposal: the old ledger stays with the old town and feeds its rift).
- Save layout for several towns (needs an ADR).
notes:
2026-09-24 DIRECTION v2 (final; GAME_SPEC § Direction). Adds to the body above; where it says SUPERSEDES, v2 wins.
V2 STEP 8 LIST: formations of actual participants, mobile districts, chapter transitions, compatible world files and cross-world politics.
- A chapter ends when the Door departs: fall, expulsion, fulfilled ambitions, chair succession or player choice. People and possessions migrate physically; other institutions and souls remain. Debts and established identities persist. [r6: buildings and stockpiles stay unless transported; people migrate only through actual departures.]
- The Founder Walks Again [r9]: a living retiree's once-per-life muster. Actual pupils travel from their institutions; every participant keeps ordinary cooldowns, locks and counter priorities; survivors go home afterwards.
- The Town Gets Up: restore the guardian's doorway, train custodians, connect staffed districts, build articulated supports. Its crews may choose evacuation over your siege.
- Later generations: former Risen hold the important chairs. A succession of personal rivalries, not anonymous resets.
- SUPERSEDES the body's OPEN proposal on what "fallen" means. GAME_SPEC § 11 PROVISIONAL now reads: fall = the roster lost beyond recovery, and expulsion (the overthrow) is a separate chapter end. Still for the owner.

BLOCKER: ARCHITECTURE NOTE 10 needs an ADR before step 8 (godot-architect; not written yet). World files: importing a world needs identities unique across files, and it extends save boundary #1. "Cannot resurrect or duplicate anyone" holds inside one continuity only, because file copying cannot enforce global custody [r1]. A divergent file's conflicting accounts can enter as testimony, never as revived or duplicated people [r9]. This joins the body's existing "save layout for several towns (needs an ADR)".

A2 ITEM ON THIS STEP:
- Reunion geography [r9, restored at full force]: kept reciprocal promises pull worlds together, and betrayal breaks the link. Escort the people whose agreement makes the crossing possible.

TWISTS (§ 14; notes only; a scoped bead comes when this step is next):
1. You Become Someone Else's Summon: a former apprentice's fulfilled covenant names the Door as its promised arrival. Your actual anchor crosses into their settlement under its charter; ordinary hero-pull weights stay unchanged. Negotiate with people who once followed you, and seek a willing representative. Links: Heralds, covenants, Old World, defiance.
2. The Multiverse Answers the Counter: schools in different worlds master complementary motifs, and reciprocal promises pull their regions into a shared formation. Ordinary casts combine into a counter against a world-scale enemy miracle, and one estranged conductor can refuse the crucial answer. Pilot a participant, coordinate the sequence, reconcile the missing voice. Links: Concordance, music, reunion geography, belief, settlements.

OPEN OWNER DECISIONS (§ 13; the director asked the owner 2026-09-24):
- A former town summons the Door: binding covenant arrival or ordinary invitation? RECOMMEND covenant arrival, placing you under the society your heroes built.
- Concordance between worlds: one coupled formation or separate allied walking cities? RECOMMEND the coupled formation, with every community keeping its agency.
2026-09-24 OWNER RULINGS (§ 13, "A all"). These SUPERSEDE the OPEN OWNER DECISIONS note above.
- A former town summons the Door (You Become Someone Else's Summon): a covenant arrival, binding ONLY if the player or their Herald agreed to it earlier. The agreement is a covenant term recorded in the Ledger by ig-m6o.5's Heralds. Without that earlier agreement, the summons is an ordinary invitation the player can decline. Scope change: the twist needs both paths, the binding arrival and a declinable invitation, plus a check that reads the earlier covenant. The Herald's promise binds only within its mandate (ig-m6o.5 Heralds).
- Concordance between worlds: one coupled formation, not separate allied walking cities. Every community keeps its agency, so one estranged conductor can still refuse (The Multiverse Answers the Counter).
- D (the Old World readings: the living stay unless they travel with the Door; "fall" = roster lost beyond recovery, separate from expulsion) stays PROVISIONAL in GAME_SPEC § 11 until this step is scoped.

title: Living-world 6: Death and power remain personal (graves, Parliament of Ghosts, hollows, Winter of Names)
description:
WHY
New feeling: grief, responsibility and discovery. Nothing ends without leaving something.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction, pillars "Power Has Witnesses" and "Nothing Ends Without Leaving Something", step 6; ruling 4 (afterlife).

SCOPE (tech-lead splits it)
- Graves you visit with friends. This is the first reader of a dead hero's Ledger history.
- Sacrifice reactions: protests, hidden victims, purposeful volunteers, and desertions that found rival towns (step 5 settlements).
- The Parliament of Ghosts: sacrificed people perform their real techniques, cooperating or resisting according to their promises.
- Hollow bosses carrying a dead hero's real kit and gear.
- The Winter of Names: unfinished dreams return to familiar homes.
- Inherited techniques. A dead defender's protection is found in their doorway.

RULING 4 (hard line)
- A dead hero is NEVER playable again: no revive and no re-summon, in the Old World too.
- Ghost visits, hollows and the Parliament are fine. They are the dead acting, not the dead back on the roster.
- kill_hero stays the only roster remover. Nothing in this step adds anyone back to the roster.

DEPENDS
Step 5.

OPEN
- The Parliament's power scale.
- Hollow difficulty.
- How often a sacrifice reaction fires (PROVISIONAL).
notes:
2026-09-24 DIRECTION v2 (final; GAME_SPEC § Direction). Adds to the body above; where it says SUPERSEDES, v2 wins.
V2 STEP 6 LIST: the soul registry, bindings, sacrifice consequences, item custody, graves, hollows, Winter, Parliament and Last Watch.
- Soul states (GAME_SPEC § 7 table): Unmoored, Resting, Parliament, Guardian, Hollow, Winter visitor, In transit, Released (terminal). One soul holds one presence; visits vacate the prior role.
- Hollows need an actual available soul and vessel. They use the dead hero's kit and preferences, with only equipment they actually hold. A remembering friend can exploit the missing-partner fallback. Victory frees the soul, never recruits the dead.
- The Last Watch: a guardian announces its final season; train a living custodian or lose the protection. Forced binding is imprisonment: the guardian may shelter residents from your enforcers before becoming the hollow you made.
- Sacrifice consequences [r3]: witnesses tell. Pupils can abandon the recipient's school, a bondmate can hide the intended donor, and former students can found a rival tradition trained to break the stolen combination. Desertions and rival towns need note 2's departure path (ig-m6o.5).
- Design principle "Personhood persists" (GAME_SPEC § Design principles): the Door carries accountability to sacrificed souls, not automatic custody of them.

BLOCKER: ARCHITECTURE NOTE 8 needs an ADR before building (godot-architect; same ADR family as note 2 on ig-m6o.5; not written yet). The soul registry is state after death, and kill_hero stays the only roster remover. Soul transitions need their own writer and Ledger kinds, and one soul holds one presence at a time.

A2 ITEM ON THIS STEP:
- Explorable dream-space [r9, restored at full force]: rooms built from participants' incompatible interpretations. Guide living dreamers through a contradiction, then test their conclusions awake. It never rewrites what happened. Dream projections are views of the same living actor, never acting copies, and that person's death ends their part (ruling 6). It sits here because it shares machinery with § 7's dream testimony; otherwise it needs only step 2's knowledge.

title: Living-world 4: Summoning with consequences (homelands, entourages, beacon pity, pursuers, living Essence)
description:
WHY
New feeling: anticipation about who arrives next. Every summon changes two worlds.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction, pillars "The Door Opens Onto Lives" and "Power Has Witnesses", step 4; ruling 2 (power source: BOTH).

SCOPE (tech-lead splits it)
- Homeland rifts and populations: a summon is glimpsed mid-adventure before rank, name, passion and dream appear. A homeland remembers who was taken from it.
- Anchors and entourage arrivals: distinct relatives, rivals and pupils, never duplicate souls.
- Beacon pity: a particular recruit approaches a guaranteed arrival. This lifts "pity system" from GAME_SPEC § Scope boundaries for this step only.
- Pursuers: extraordinary power arrives with the one who knows how to beat it.
- A homeland can demand its missing person back.
- Living Essence and deed promotion (ruling 2):
  - Living deeds and achievements, read from the Ledger, earn Essence.
  - Deeds can also rank a hero up directly. That is the Risen path, F->SSS by deeds.
  - Sacrifice stays the fast, dark path.
  - Finished dreams and Founding pay in step 5.

SPINE (flag; no formula ships until this is done)
Living Essence moves the ~327-pull spine and the 15x "manufacture, don't pray" ratio. game-designer restates SYSTEMS § Sacrifice -> rank up with both sources before any formula ships. Proposed guardrails (PROVISIONAL):
- Living Essence never makes Summon Stones.
- Per hour of play, sacrifice stays the fastest route to SSS. Living routes are slower, but the hero is kept.
- A deed rank-up is a milestone, never a farm.
- The owner signs off on the restated spine.

DEPENDS
Step 3. Beacon pity needs P2-09's stone income, already ruled.

OPEN
- The shape of homeland populations (they are not town NPCs).
- The pity numbers.
- Pursuer frequency.
- Whether dupes/resonance (same class) survives "no duplicate souls" unchanged. Game-designer reading: yes, a same-class hero is not the same soul, but the name "dupe" goes.
notes:
2026-09-24 DIRECTION v2 (final; GAME_SPEC § Direction). Adds to the body above; where it says SUPERSEDES, v2 wins.
V2 STEP 4 LIST: rank/identity selection, chorus, pity identity, crossings, deed rewards, Essence provenance and belief manifestations.
- The chorus [r3]: roll ordinary rank from the unchanged weights, then the town's conversation influences WHICH eligible person answers. Each resident's influence is bounded, weighted by conviction, recall and connection; one speaker cannot drown out the town. It never selects a product.
- Crossings: summoning removes someone from a world whose dependents, rivals and pursuers can follow.
- Belief manifestations [r2]: distinct believers, conviction and remembered salience drive whisper -> legend -> miracle (a motif, then a usable skill, then a transformed battlefield effect). Copying testimony adds no believers. Contradictory claims can manifest competing powers. The hero's stance can refuse a miracle. A false legend can inspire a real undertaking; after exposure comes a Trial of the Boast.
- Pulled in from step 1: Essence provenance lands here (GAME_SPEC § 10 PROVISIONAL).

SUPERSEDES the body's "Deeds can also rank a hero up directly. That is the Risen path." v2 § 4: deeds earn Essence (each milestone pays once), and rank-ups spend Essence. RISEN = born F, reached SSS, with a personal ascent deed before every promotion. Either Essence source can fund the cost; sacrifice cannot supply the deed. Unwitnessed achievements count; retelling never mints Essence again. The SYSTEMS spine flag now says the same.

ARCHITECTURE NOTE 5: the pity traveler is an explicit exception to ordinary rank weights, and no topic can erase it. game-designer owns the threshold.
ARCHITECTURE NOTE 6: living Essence never makes Stones; sacrifice stays the fastest route to SSS per hour; Concordance keeps the x3 on a practised shared technique (ig-m6o.3).

A2 ITEMS ON THIS STEP:
1. Held the Bridge [r2], the worked legend skill: a spectral crossing whose defender intercepts attacks on those passing behind. Greater manifestation extends what it protects. It keeps a cooldown and the ability lock. Residents reenact it with lanterns; a confession changes the performance (some lanterns go out, others form a new emblem). A nemesis can attack both ends of the crossing to force a visible choice. It rides on step 3's Legend eligibility rule.
2. Plants [r4]: captors route a real agent through a summon. The spy reports only what they learn, and needs a messenger, a meeting or a rift to send it. Witnesses can expose them; friendship can make them hold back, or turn them. The player may know before residents do, but exposure still needs reaching them. Needs step 2's knowledge.

OPEN, added: what triggers resonance once Concordance takes the x3 (SYSTEMS § Dupes and resonance, Amended).
2026-09-24 director ruling (GAME_SPEC § 10, folded 2026-09-24): the § 10 PROVISIONAL is settled. Essence provenance lands here with its first reader. The earlier "(GAME_SPEC § 10 PROVISIONAL)" pointer now means that ruling.

title: Living-world 5: Ambitions become institutions (Founding, apprentices, seasons, raids, settlements)
description:
WHY
New feeling: pride in a society with its own future. Ambitions become institutions.
Spec: GAME_SPEC.md § Direction, pillar "A Home Worth Returning To" and step 5; ruling 2 (Founding earns Essence).

SCOPE (tech-lead splits it)
- Founding: a finished dream founds a tavern, school or forge that seeds other people's dreams. Founding and finished dreams earn Essence (ruling 2). This amends "the town never makes Summon Stones, Essence or parts" (GAME_SPEC § The town builder) for Essence only. Stones and parts stay expedition-only.
- Apprentices and collaborative schools. A retiree trains pupils.
- Food pressure and seasons: feed households through winter; design evacuation routes around real rescue promises. This lifts "day/night, weather" from § Scope boundaries for seasons only.
- Raids on the town ("defend the town", which had no slice until now).
- Independent settlements: grown apprentices or deserters found towns that reinterpret your traditions. They are places you can visit.

READS THE LEDGER
Dreams, deeds, apprenticeships and meals.

DEPENDS
Step 4 (the living-Essence spine must be restated first).

OPEN (game-designer)
- The Founding Essence amounts (spine-checked).
- The season length on the live clock. Nothing ages while the game is closed (hard constraint).
- Raid frequency.
notes:
2026-09-24 DIRECTION v2 (final; GAME_SPEC § Direction). Adds to the body above; where it says SUPERSEDES, v2 wins.
V2 STEP 5 LIST: teaching, recipes, ownership, jobs, seasonal production, living roster exits, settlements, covenants, Herald mandates and collective projects.
- Heralds [r9]: a hero accepts the Door's Voice and a public mandate. An authorised promise creates a covenant binding the Door (speaker, beneficiaries, terms and mandate recorded). Revoking the Herald does not erase promises already made. A forbidden promise records an attempted overstep; it cannot transfer a soul or award a rank. Your Herald can grant sanctuary to the nemesis you meant to kill.
- Settlements [r9]: an apprentice's founding ambition gains collaborators, resources and a reachable site. People physically migrate with their identities, possessions and relationships, and their charter gives them authority independent of the Door.
- Recipes: rift potlucks spread recipes; learned dishes become food and expedition provisions.
- Pulled in from step 1: item identities land here, with ownership (GAME_SPEC § 10 PROVISIONAL).

BLOCKER: ARCHITECTURE NOTES 2 AND 7 need an ADR before building. godot-architect's call; not written yet.
- Note 2, living roster exits: desertion, rival-town founding, defection, settlement migration and taking the Guest's chair all remove a LIVING hero, and some can reverse. Boundary #3 says kill_hero() is the only remover. Before any of them is built, an ADR adds one audited departure path that writes its own Ledger kind. Death stays kill_hero-only. This is the first step that needs it.
- Note 7, new roster entries (same ADR as note 2): The Person Nobody Summoned enters without summon_hero, the summoned kind's one writer. It needs its own entry path and Ledger kind. It must be rare and costly, so belief never becomes a free summon (number: game designer).

A2 ITEMS ON THIS STEP:
1. Memory-forged items [r1]: an object keeps the event it took part in, and witnesses disagree about what it means. Forge a response to a failure you admit; recover another storied object. FLAG: "forge" touches the "crafting trees" exclusion (GAME_SPEC § Scope boundaries). This ticket must rule whether it is one.
2. Pressures are approaching choices [r4], in live time only. Winter: falling temperature closes production and approaches the Winter of Names; stock food, keep a promised route open. Hunger: reserves collide with household commitments; residents share rations, conceal a shortage or contest distribution, and food is conserved through every transfer. Raids: enemies pick reachable objectives from acquired knowledge and grudges; a spy who knows the evacuation route makes its defence urgent.
3. The battlefield band [r9, restored at full force]: taught call-and-response motifs. Completing the sequence makes a particular counter applicable, and it still needs its ordinary cast and timing. Assemble performers from different traditions. It rides on step 3's eligibility rules.
4. Profession dreams' payoffs [r4] (the dreams themselves are ig-m6o.2): a bridgewright school, a school teaching the paired shield technique, a Hall of Witnesses.

TWIST: The Person Nobody Summoned (§ 14). A note only; a scoped bead comes when this step is next. A recurring fictional character gains sincere belief until a miracle gives them a new life. The Ledger records their birth now, not the stories' past. They are a mortal person with their own dream. Links: authored accounts, belief (ig-m6o.4), Founding, dreams. Needs note 7's entry path.

OPEN OWNER DECISION (§ 13; the director asked the owner 2026-09-24): is the miracle-born person a genuinely new mortal person, or an embodied construct? RECOMMEND the person, with a new identity and no invented past.
2026-09-24 OWNER RULING (§ 13, "A all"). This SUPERSEDES the OPEN OWNER DECISION note above.
- The miracle-born person (The Person Nobody Summoned) is a genuinely new mortal person, not an embodied construct: a new identity, no invented past. It is rare and costly. game-designer sets how rare and what it costs before the twist is scoped.
- Also (ruling 2, lands in ig-m6o.8): a former town's summons binds the Door only if the player or their Herald agreed to it earlier. So this step's Herald covenants must be able to record that agreement as an ordinary covenant term: who promised, to which settlement, under which mandate. ig-m6o.8 reads it. No new mechanism, just a term the covenant record can hold.
- § 10 PROVISIONAL settled (director ruling): item identities land here with ownership. The earlier "(GAME_SPEC § 10 PROVISIONAL)" pointer now means that ruling.

title: A dispatch-time ability_auto policy never reaches battle actors
description: Found in ig-gy0.1 (Sol confirmed): create_run builds actors from the team snapshot, so an order's policies.ability_auto set at dispatch is never read; the sim only ever read the actor's own flag (set later by command). gy0.1 migrates old checkpoints from the actor field, which is correct. Decide: either the policy seeds each actor's skill modes at create_run, or the policy field is dead and gets removed. Touches save boundary #1 (orders).
close_reason: Moot since ig-gy0.3 (890c13a). New orders never write the ability_auto policy; each actor's skill modes come from the snapshot. Orders saved before gy0.3 keep their unapplied policy values, as they always did. Those orders are transient and settle soon, so applying the old values isn't worth the code.

The fuller MMO feel the owner described: "basically play an mmo character". Later than ig-gy0.6 on purpose.

title: Town builder 5: food, farms, and starvation (warned, never offline)
description:
WHY
In Banished, food is the thing you manage. The owner, 2026-09-23: "They eat and can starve to death." This was chosen knowingly, against our recommendation (hunger only slows work). So the town becomes a second way to lose a hero, and it has to be fair: a death is never a surprise and never happens while you are not looking.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § Heroes eat, and can starve to death. Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Food and starvation (all PROVISIONAL). Boundaries: DECISIONS.md "2026-09-23: The town builder", item 11, and ARCHITECTURE.md rule 8's amendment (both accepted 2026-09-23).

RULED (do not reopen)
- Only housed heroes who are home eat. Away (dispatched) and busy (in a battle) heroes don't eat, and unhoused heroes never do. Unhousing a hero stops its eating: that is the escape hatch.
- Nothing happens while the game is closed. Food and the starvation clock move only on the live tick (_advance_clocks_in_memory), never in the offline catch-up.
- Every death is warned. A ladder of warnings; the clock stops at a last warning until the player acknowledges; one death at a time.
- The victim is the eater with the lowest rank, then the lowest level, then the newest in the roster.
- kill_hero() is the only removal (rule 8). The victim's gear goes to inventory first, so no Lost Cache. The Ledger has landed: starvation passes cause "starvation".
- Draughts do not cost food in v1 (game-designer, 2026-09-23; SYSTEMS "Food does not make draughts (v1)").
- The first Farm is free: the Farm joins FREE_FIRST (ig-6m2.10).
- Starving multiplies each workplace's final rate, after ig-6m2.7's skill bonus when that lands.
- A Farm under construction makes nothing and takes no worker. ig-6m2.3.2's rule covers every workplace type, so nothing here is needed for it.

SPLIT (tech-lead, 2026-09-24)
Two slices, in order, one implementer pass each. The parent closes when both close. ig-m6o.2.2 waits on .5.1 only: shared meals need food and eating, not starvation (re-pointed 2026-09-24).
- ig-6m2.5.1, farms and food: the Farm, food as a saved resource, eating. Food at 0 does nothing more yet.
- ig-6m2.5.2, starvation: the clock, the half-speed work, the warning ladder, the deaths. It gets its own boundary #1 and #3 review.

DEPENDS ON ig-6m2.3.1 only, not construction (re-pointed 2026-09-24). Food copies the Mine's second-resource pattern: a type in TownRules, a town_resources key, a count of workers home by type, the type-driven placed panel line and the resource label. It also edits the same functions, so it must not run in parallel with .3.1.

ASSETS (no download)
building_grain (neutral\) from the owner-approved KayKit Medieval Hexagon Pack 1.0 FREE, already unzipped at C:\Users\Joony\AppData\Local\Temp\kaykit\town\KayKit_Medieval_Hexagon_Pack_1.0_FREE\Assets\gltf\buildings\neutral\. Copy the .gltf and its .bin flat into hub/town/models/hexagon/. The windmill is not staged. If that Temp folder is gone, stop and ask the director.

NON-GOALS
cooking or recipes (a crafting tree); seasons and cold; per-hero hunger meters; anything while the game is closed; food for draughts; a second use for food.
notes:
2026-09-23 game-designer, settled ahead of the slice:
- Item 9 is DECIDED: draughts do NOT cost food in v1. They keep their F-parts cost. Drop item 9. SYSTEMS.md § Food and starvation, "Food does not make draughts (v1)", gives the four reasons. The main one: a hungry town must not also cut the revival draughts that save heroes.
- The first Farm is free (SYSTEMS § "The first of each producer is free"). That is the way out of starvation with no wood.
- Starving applies to the final rate, after the worker skill bonus (ig-6m2.7): base * (1 + 0.10*skill) * starving_work_multiplier.
- A Farm under construction (ig-6m2.3) makes nothing and takes no worker.
- The town ADR and rule 8's amendment are ACCEPTED (2026-09-23). The body's "PROPOSED" wording is stale.
2026-09-24 game-designer, cross-lane: the Ledger (ig-m6o.1, ADR PROPOSED 2026-09-24) gives kill_hero optional cause/by arguments and writes a 'died' record there. If the Ledger has landed when this slice does, starvation passes cause starvation. If this slice lands first, ig-m6o.1 adds it.
2026-09-24 tech-lead: re-pointed from the whole ig-6m2.3 to ig-6m2.3.1. Food copies the Mine's second-resource pattern and edits the same functions, but needs no construction: ig-6m2.3.2 gives every workplace type a build time, so a Farm is covered whichever lands first. Split into ig-6m2.5.1 (farms and food) and ig-6m2.5.2 (starvation, its own boundary #1/#3 review). Item 9 (draughts) is gone, per the game-designer note. SYSTEMS gained one sentence: starving means the clock is above 0 (no half/full flicker).

title: Idle spawn facing points away from the fight (enemies down, allies up)
description: Finding from ig-oit (2026-09-23). After ig-oit, attackers in range face their targets, but units that have not yet engaged keep their spawn facing: enemies spawn facing DOWN, allies facing UP, both away from the fight. Consider spawning each side facing the other. This changes idle-flank odds for rogue _is_behind again (an idle target facing away gives a free rear bonus today), so it is a design call on rogue power, not just a visual fix. Route: game-designer rules, then a 1-2 line sim change + test.
notes:
2026-09-24 check: BLOCKED on a game-designer ruling, as the bead's own route says. No code changed.
- docs/SYSTEMS.md, DECISIONS.md and KNOWN_ISSUES.md have no spawn-facing ruling.

title: Boss stagger meter (elites): hits fill it, full meter staggers/stuns

title: Carry rule mismatch: SYSTEMS says one uninterrupted second, code pauses and resumes
description: Found by designer on ig-n9r (2026-09-23). SYSTEMS.md:~177 says carrying a downed ally 'takes one uninterrupted second'. battle_simulation.gd:1016-1019 _update_carry pauses progress when the carrier leaves the 1.5 range and resumes later; nothing resets it. Knockback (ig-n9r) will make the gap show up more. Needs a game-designer call on which is right, then a code or doc fix.
notes:
DESIGNER RULING (2026-09-24): the code's pause/resume is right, the doc was wrong. SYSTEMS.md now says it: carry needs one second of channeling within 1.5 of the body, not one unbroken second. Leaving range (push, dodge), a stun or a root pauses it; it resumes where it stopped. Why: a push never interrupts (Knockback), and with a restart rule a crit push every second (the crit gate's cap) or a stun chain could block a rescue for good. The doc fix is uncommitted in docs/SYSTEMS.md (Knockback "Carry" bullet + Downed heroes and rescue).

CODE HALF (high1, after ig-wgj.10). One gap: progress is not tied to its body. The rule: carry_progress belongs to one (carrier, body) pair and starts over on a new body, or when the carrier is downed. Two leaks today, both in combat/battle/battle_simulation.gd:
1. Rescue auto-battle AI (~476-500): each planning pass clears order_target_id on non-direct actors and re-picks _nearest_unassigned_downed. If a different body is now nearest (a newly downed ally, or the carrier dodged), the carrier keeps the old progress and can lift the new body after less than a second. Fix: keep the previous order_kind/order_target_id before the clear. Erase effect_state.carry_progress unless the new pick is COMMAND_CARRY on that same body. This covers the retreat branches too.
2. Downing (~1686-1693, ally branch): the downed carrier keeps order_kind carry, order_target_id and carry_progress. After a revive (_revive_actor ~1628) the AI can re-issue carry with stale progress. Fix: erase carry_progress in the ally-downed branch. One place; no revive change needed.
Already right, leave alone: the carry command sets 0.0 (~221), _replace_direct_order erases it (~1881), _update_carry erases it when the body is revived or taken (~1716).

SEAMS
- Save #1: no shape change. carry_progress is already optional in effect_state (battle_actor.gd:235) and saved via to_dict. Erasing it is legal, and legacy checkpoints load unchanged. Add no new key (no stored carry_target_id: the previous order_target_id is enough).
- Combat #4: only BattleSimulation models downed/carry. QuickResolve and arena.gd resolve(team, wave) have no carry, so nothing lands there.
- Golden: test_pre_skills_checkpoint_loads_migrates_and_finishes_identically is a standard battle with no carry. The AI carry branch runs only when state.kind == "rescue", and the down-site erase is a no-op without the key. So the expected.json must NOT move. If it moves, the fix is wrong; don't re-record it.

TESTS (tests/unit/test_battle_rescue.gd)
1. Pause/resume: channel 0.5 s, push the carrier beyond 1.5 (set position), advance 0.5 s: progress still 0.5. Walk back: the lift lands after about 0.5 s more in range, not 1.0.
2. Stun pauses: stun mid-channel, and progress holds through the stun, then resumes.
3. AI re-target starts at 0: rescue auto-battle, carrier at 0.6 s on body A. Down a nearer ally B so the AI re-picks B: progress resets, and B lifts only after a full 1.0 s.
4. Same body keeps progress: across planning passes with no nearer body, progress accumulates and the lift lands at 1.0 s (guards against a fix that resets every pass).
5. Down clears it: carrier at 0.6 s is downed, so carry_progress is absent. Revive it and let the AI re-carry: a full 1.0 s.
6. Save mid-channel: to_dict → JSON → from_dict at 0.5 s, and the lift lands after 0.5 s more (the existing save seam, now pinned).
7. BUILT + full GUT, with the golden unchanged.
Review: boundary #1 is untouched, but it touches the combat sim; Sol read-only per repo rules.

The code half goes to high1 after ig-wgj.10 and ig-wgj.12 (the P1s go first). The SYSTEMS doc half gets committed with the next BUILT.

description:
Direction, not a ticket. The largest of the four by a wide margin. Walk out of the town gate into an instanced map with objectives and play the run. Sent expeditions stay math and are not replaced.

Cannot become a ticket until these are answered: what an objective is, how a run ends, whether the instance is authored or generated (GAME_SPEC.md 'Scope boundaries' deliberately excludes procedural generation from the draft), and how a played run reports through CombatResult without anything upstream branching on which path produced it.
